對，Charmbracelet / Charm 基本上是「把 CLI/TUI 做得很漂亮」這條路線的代表團隊之一。它不是只做幾個 CLI，而是做了一整套 Go-based terminal UI 生態系：框架、元件、樣式、Markdown renderer、SSH TUI、腳本 UI、小工具、demo 錄製、甚至 AI coding agent。GitHub org 目前有 54 個 repo，很多都還很活躍。 ￼

我會把它分成幾層看：

1. 做 TUI App 的核心框架

最核心是這幾個：

專案    用途    感覺像
Bubble Tea    Go 的 TUI framework，類 Elm architecture    React/Redux 但在 terminal
Bubbles    Bubble Tea 的元件庫    input、textarea、spinner、list、table
Lip Gloss    terminal styling/layout    CSS for terminal
Glamour    Markdown renderer    給 CLI app 內嵌漂亮 Markdown
Huh    Terminal forms    表單、選項、confirm 等

Charm 官網也把 Bubble Tea、Huh、Lip Gloss、Wish、Glamour、Bubbles、Log、Harmonica 放在主要技術線上。 ￼

這套的厲害點是：
它不是「用 ncurses 寫很硬的 TUI」，而是比較現代化的狀態更新模型。Bubble Tea 是 model / update / view 風格，Lip Gloss 則像用 CSS 一樣定義 terminal layout。Charm 自己說 Bubble Tea 已被用在數千個 app 裡，Lip Gloss 也被大量 CLI/TUI 工具採用。 ￼

如果你想寫 Go CLI/TUI，這條線很值得學。

⸻

2. 給 shell script 用的「不用寫 Go」工具

最實用的是 gum。

gum 可以讓 shell script 直接有漂亮的互動介面，例如：

choice=$(gum choose "train" "test" "backtest" "deploy")
name=$(gum input --placeholder "experiment name")
gum confirm "Run now?" && ./run.sh

Charm 官網說 gum 是把 Bubbles + Lip Gloss 的能力包成單一 binary，讓 shell script / aliases 不用寫 Go 也能用漂亮的 input、selection、layout。 ￼

對你的 dotfiles / ML experiment / backtest runner 其實很有用，例如：

task=$(gum choose "download-data" "train-model" "run-backtest" "open-dashboard")
date=$(gum input --placeholder "2026-04-29")
gum spin --title "Running $task..." -- python scripts/$task.py --date "$date"

它很適合做：

scripts/
  run_experiment.sh
  choose_env.sh
  deploy_streamlit.sh
  pueue_submit.sh
  select_mlflow_run.sh

尤其你常做 CLI automation，gum 應該是 Charm 裡面最馬上能用上的。

⸻

3. Markdown / 文件 / demo 相關工具

這幾個也很有代表性：

專案    用途
Glow    CLI Markdown reader
VHS    用 script 錄 terminal demo，輸出 GIF / video
Freeze    把 code / terminal output 轉成圖片
Glamour    給 Go app 內嵌 Markdown renderer

Glow 是一個 terminal Markdown reader，Charm 官網稱它有 CLI + TUI 介面，可以漂亮地讀 Markdown。 ￼
VHS 則是「CLI home video recorder」，可以用 tape/script 描述 terminal 操作，產生 README 裡常見的 terminal GIF。GitHub repo 也顯示 VHS 是他們非常受歡迎的專案之一。 ￼

對你這種會寫 README、dotfiles、agent workflow 文件的人，這幾個很有用：

glow README.md
vhs demo.tape
freeze main.py --output code.png

⸻

4. SSH / remote-first CLI app

這條線我覺得很有 Charm 特色：

專案    用途
Wish    用 Go 寫 SSH app
Soft Serve    self-hosted Git server with TUI
Skate    personal key-value store

Charm 的理念是：CLI 不一定要靠 HTTP API，也可以用 SSH key 當身份系統，然後直接把 TUI stream 給遠端使用者。Wish 就是用來做這種 SSH app 的框架，Soft Serve 則是用 SSH/Git/TUI 做出來的自架 Git server。 ￼

這跟你常聊的 SSH + tmux + remote dev 其實蠻對味。它的想法不是「在瀏覽器重做一套 IDE」，而是「terminal 本身就是 UI runtime」。

⸻

5. 新一代 AI / agent 線

比較新的方向包括：

專案    用途
Crush    agentic coding CLI
Catwalk    LLM inference providers/models collection
Fantasy    Go 裡 build AI agents，多 provider/model API
Mods    CLI interface to LLMs

GitHub repo 列表裡，crush 目前描述是 “Glamourous agentic coding for all”，星數已經很高，而且最近仍有更新。 ￼
Charm 官網也把 Mods 描述成「CLI interface to the world’s best models」。 ￼

這條線可以跟你之前研究的 Claude Code / OpenCode / Codex CLI / Cursor CLI 放在一起比較。Charm 的特色大概會是：UI/UX 很 terminal-native，Go single binary，重視漂亮 TUI。但 agent 能力本身要另外評估，不能只看它 UI 很帥。

⸻

我會怎麼評價 Charm

Charm 最強的地方不是單一工具，而是它把 terminal tooling 做成一套完整美學和工程風格：

Go TUI app:
Bubble Tea + Bubbles + Lip Gloss + Glamour + Huh
Shell script:
gum
README/demo:
vhs + freeze + glow
Remote/SSH app:
wish + soft-serve
AI/agent:
crush + mods + catwalk/fantasy

對你來說，最值得優先玩的順序我會排：

1. gum：馬上改善 shell scripts / dotfiles / backtest runner UX
2. glow：讀 Markdown 很舒服，也適合 README 預覽
3. vhs / freeze：做 CLI demo、README GIF、截圖
4. Bubble Tea + Lip Gloss：如果你真的要寫 Go TUI app
5. Wish / Soft Serve：如果你想做 SSH-first app 或自架 Git/TUI
6. Crush / Mods：放進 AI coding agent 工具鏈裡觀察

你可以先裝這幾個：

brew install gum glow vhs freeze

然後先試一個很實用的：

#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
cmd=$(gum choose "train" "backtest" "mlflow-ui" "streamlit")
date=$(gum input --placeholder "date, e.g. 2026-04-29")
gum confirm "Run $cmd for $date?" || exit 0
gum spin --title "Running $cmd..." -- bash -c "
  echo Running $cmd for $date
  sleep 2
"

我的感覺是：Charmbracelet 是 CLI/TUI 世界裡少數真的有產品審美的團隊。很多 CLI 工具是「能用就好」，Charm 是「terminal 也應該漂亮、互動自然、能產品化」。對你這種常在 terminal 裡工作、又喜歡 dotfiles/automation/agent workflow 的人，確實很值得研究。
```

The repo uses **three-layer cross-platform strategy**:

**Layer 3: GitHub releases fallback (user-level, no sudo)**
- When system package fails or unavailable

Now I have a comprehensive view of the codebase. Let me compile my findings into a clear report:

---

## Gum UX Improvement Opportunities — Dotfiles Survey

Based on systematic review of tmux menus, shell scripts, and chezmoi automation, here are concrete places where `gum` could improve UX:

### 1. **tmux/ — Hard-coded Display Menus (Row-Limited)**

**File:** `executable_menu.sh` (line 70)
- **Current UX:** `tmux display-menu` with tier-based visibility to work around 14-row height limit
- **Why gum helps:** `gum choose` has no height ceiling; the entire tier0+tier1+tier2 menu could be unified into a single rich picker with better UX when terminal is tall
- **Sketch:** `gum choose --header "tmux menu" --height 30 "Last window" "Last pane" "Choose window" ... | xargs tmux`
- **Note:** Replacement would be **alongside** (keep tmux bindings, add gum as progressive enhancement)

**File:** `executable_menu-theme.sh` (line 4)
- **Current UX:** Hard-coded 2-row `display-menu` for theme switching (catppuccin vs tmux2k)
- **Why gum helps:** `gum choose` would render the same but is cleaner as the list grows
- **Sketch:** `gum choose --header "Pick theme" "catppuccin" "tmux2k" | xargs -I{} tmux set -g @theme_variant {} && ...`
- **Replacement:** **Substitute** (simpler than menu.sh alternative)

**File:** `executable_menu-session.sh` (line 4)
- **Current UX:** Hard-coded tmux `command-prompt` for rename, break-pane, etc.
- **Why gum:** `gum input` + `gum confirm` could replace the prompts for better styling and validation
- **Sketch:** Session renaming: `gum input --placeholder "new name" | xargs -I{} tmux rename-session -- {}`

### 2. **scripts/import_ssh_to_bw.sh — Interactive Menu Selection**

**File:** `import_ssh_to_bw.sh` (line 182–229)
- **Current UX:** `read -r choice` with manual parsing for "1 3 4" or "a" (lines 192, 216)
- **Why gum helps:** `gum choose --no-limit` would provide checkboxes, search, and preview instead of manual text entry
- **Sketch:** 
  ```bash
  gum choose --no-limit --header "Select keys to import" \
    "1: id_rsa" "2: github_key" "3: work_key" | \
    awk '{print $1}' | tr -d ':' | while read i; do import_key "${keys[$((i-1))]}"; done
  ```
- **Replacement:** **Substitute** (cleaner UX, no need for loop/validation)

**File:** Same file (line 258)
- **Current UX:** `read -r overwrite` for yes/no confirmation
- **Why gum:** `gum confirm` is purpose-built for this
- **Sketch:** `gum confirm "Overwrite existing item?" && bw delete ...`

### 3. **scripts/upgrade_tools.sh — Category Selection**

**File:** `upgrade_tools.sh` (lines 84–177)
- **Current UX:** CLI args only (`--only a,b,c` or positional `scripts/upgrade_tools.sh brew mise`)
- **Gap:** No interactive category picker when called without args; just defaults to `all`
- **Why gum:** Could offer interactive category selection with `gum choose --no-limit` for multi-select
- **Sketch:**
  ```bash
  if [[ ${#SELECTED[@]} -eq 0 ]]; then
    SELECTED=($(gum choose --no-limit --header "Select categories to upgrade" \
      externals brew mise uv npm cargo dotnet gem flatpak warp agents plugins))
  fi
  ```
- **Replacement:** **Additive** (existing CLI remains untouched, interactive path added)

### 4. **scripts/fleet_apply.py — No UX, Pure CLI**

**File:** `fleet_apply.py` (lines 405–418 in justfile)
- **Current UX:** Python script with `--hosts`, `--branch`, `--serial` flags only
- **Gap:** No interactive host picker when inventory is large; you must memorize names or `grep` the TOML
- **Why gum:** `gum choose` (via subprocess) could list machines from machines.toml and let you pick subset
- **Sketch:** Python wrapper could call `gum choose --no-limit` to populate `--hosts` automatically
- **Note:** Would require Python → bash subprocess (feasible but architectural change)

### 5. **zsh/tools/ — Already Using fzf Effectively**

**Files:** `11_tools_picker.zsh`, `12_television.zsh`, `10_fzf.zsh`
- **Finding:** These are fzf-based pickers with keybindings and previews
- **Assessment:** `gum` is not an improvement here; fzf's binding system and preview window are tighter for ZLE widgets

---

### **Summary Table (5 Candidates)**

| File | Line | UX Primitive | Gum Improvement | Type |
|------|------|--------------|-----------------|------|
| `menu.sh` | 70 | `display-menu` (tier-based) | `gum choose` (unlimited height) | alongside |
| `menu-theme.sh` | 4 | `display-menu` (2 rows) | `gum choose` (cleaner) | substitute |
| `import_ssh_to_bw.sh` | 192 | `read` + manual parse | `gum choose --no-limit` | substitute |
| `import_ssh_to_bw.sh` | 258 | `read` (y/n) | `gum confirm` | substitute |
| `upgrade_tools.sh` | 154 | CLI args only | `gum choose --no-limit` (interactive) | additive |

**Not recommended:** `fleet_apply.py` (Python, gum requires subprocess), `zsh/tools/` (fzf already optimal).

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# upgrade_tools.sh — explicit, opt-in upgrade entrypoint.
3	#
4	# `chezmoi apply` is deliberately conservative (install-only, `state: present`,
5	# `creates:` idempotency). This script is the companion upgrade path: run it
6	# (or `just upgrade-*`) when you want to actually move tools forward.
7	#
8	# Design: each category is best-effort. A failure in one category does NOT
9	# abort later categories; a summary is printed at the end listing SUCCESS /
10	# FAILED / SKIPPED categories.
11	#
12	# Usage:
13	#   scripts/upgrade_tools.sh [all|<category> ...] [flags]
14	#
15	# Categories (also selectable via `all`):
16	#   externals brew mise uv npm cargo dotnet gem agents plugins
17	#
18	# Flags:
19	#   --dry-run          Print commands without executing.
20	#   --only a,b,c       Only run listed categories (comma-separated).
21	#   --skip a,b         Run everything except listed categories.
22	#   -h, --help         Show help.
23	#
24	# See docs/this_repo/upgrades.md and `## Upgrades` in AGENTS.md for rationale.
25	
26	set -u
27	# NOTE: we deliberately do not `set -e`. Each command is guarded by _run /
28	# run_category so we can continue past individual failures.
29	
30	# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
31	# Colors + loggers (match the style used in run_onchange_after_*.sh.tmpl)
32	# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
33	if [[ -t 1 ]]; then
34	  _C_RED='\033[0;31m'
35	  _C_GRN='\033[0;32m'
36	  _C_YLW='\033[1;33m'
37	  _C_BLU='\033[0;34m'
38	  _C_DIM='\033[2m'
39	  _C_RST='\033[0m'
40	else
41	  _C_RED='' _C_GRN='' _C_YLW='' _C_BLU='' _C_DIM='' _C_RST=''
42	fi
43	
44	info() { printf '%b\n' "${_C_BLU}[INFO]${_C_RST} $*"; }
45	success() { printf '%b\n' "${_C_GRN}[SUCCESS]${_C_RST} $*"; }
46	warn() { printf '%b\n' "${_C_YLW}[WARN]${_C_RST} $*"; }
47	error() { printf '%b\n' "${_C_RED}[ERROR]${_C_RST} $*" >&2; }
48	hr() { printf '%b\n' "${_C_DIM}────────────────────────────────────────────${_C_RST}"; }
49	
50	# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
51	# Source shared sudo helper (same file used by run_*.sh.tmpl via `include`)
52	# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
53	_REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
54	# shellcheck source=lib/sudo_shared.sh
55	if [[ -f "$_REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/sudo_shared.sh" ]]; then
56	  # shellcheck disable=SC1091
57	  source "$_REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/sudo_shared.sh"
58	fi
59	
60	# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
61	# Homebrew PATH detection (mirrors .chezmoiscripts/global/run_onchange_after_30_brew_bundle.sh.tmpl)
62	# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
63	setup_brew_path() {
64	  if command -v brew >/dev/null 2>&1; then
65	    return 0
66	  fi
67	  local candidates=(
68	    /opt/homebrew/bin/brew              # macOS Apple Silicon
69	    /usr/local/bin/brew                 # macOS Intel
70	    /home/linuxbrew/.linuxbrew/bin/brew # Linuxbrew system-wide
71	    "$HOME/.linuxbrew/bin/brew"         # Linuxbrew user
72	  )
73	  for b in "${candidates[@]}"; do
74	    if [[ -x "$b" ]]; then
75	      eval "$("$b" shellenv)"
76	      return 0
77	    fi
78	  done
79	  return 1
80	}
81	
82	# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
83	# Argument parsing
84	# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
85	DRY_RUN=0
86	ONLY=""
87	SKIP=""
88	SELECTED=()
89	
90	ALL_CATEGORIES=(externals brew mise uv npm cargo dotnet gem flatpak warp agents plugins)
91	
92	usage() {
93	  cat <<EOF
94	Usage: scripts/upgrade_tools.sh [all|<category> ...] [--dry-run] [--only a,b] [--skip a,b]
95	
96	Categories: ${ALL_CATEGORIES[*]}
97	
98	Run order for 'all': ${ALL_CATEGORIES[*]}

100	Examples:

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# Top-level tmux popup menu — invoked by `prefix + Space`.
3	#
4	# Why a script (not inline `display-menu` in keybindings.conf):
5	#   1. tmux's command parser stops at literal `;`, `{`, `}` even inside
6	#      nested quotes. With ~50 menu rows full of fzf binds and shell
7	#      one-liners, escaping became fragile and broke silently.
8	#   2. tmux `display-menu` does not paginate. If the menu is taller than
9	#      the terminal, the entire popup is suppressed with no error. By
10	#      generating the menu here we can read $TMUX client_height and
11	#      auto-trim low-frequency rows when small.
12	#   3. Submenus are normal `tmux display-menu` invocations from rows;
13	#      they don't share quoting context with the parent menu.
14	#
15	# Submenus live in sibling scripts:
16	#   menu-layouts.sh, menu-session.sh, menu-sesh.sh,
17	#   menu-popups.sh, menu-theme.sh, menu-system.sh, menu-agents.sh
18	#
19	# See: pitfalls/tmux-display-menu-silent-parse-failure.md
20	
21	set -euo pipefail
22	
23	H=$(tmux display-message -p '#{client_height}')
24	DIR=~/.config/tmux
25	
26	# Tier 0: ALWAYS shown (highest frequency, ~7 rows + 2 separators)
27	declare -a tier0=(
28	  "Last window"  Tab "last-window"
29	  "Last pane"    P   "last-pane"
30	  ""             ""  ""
31	  "Choose win"   w   "choose-tree -Zw"
32	  "Choose sess"  s   "choose-tree -Zs"
33	  "Pane #s"      q   "display-panes -d 0"
34	  ""             ""  ""
35	  "Sesh picker"  g   "run-shell '$DIR/sesh-picker.sh'"
36	  "Lazygit"      G   "display-popup -E -w 90% -h 90% -d '#{pane_current_path}' -T ' lazygit ' 'lazygit'"
37	)
38	
39	# Tier 1: shown when height >= 22 (adds new-window/split/zoom)
40	declare -a tier1=(
41	  ""             ""  ""
42	  "New window"   c   "new-window -c '#{pane_current_path}'"
43	  "Split |"      "|" "split-window -h -c '#{pane_current_path}'"
44	  "Split -"      "-" "split-window -v -c '#{pane_current_path}'"
45	  "Zoom"         z   "resize-pane -Z"
46	)
47	
48	# Tier 2: submenus + cheatsheet (always shown if Tier 1 is shown)
49	declare -a tier2=(
50	  ""             ""  ""
51	  "→ Layouts"    L   "run-shell '$DIR/menu-layouts.sh'"
52	  "→ Session"    S   "run-shell '$DIR/menu-session.sh'"
53	  "→ Sesh+"      E   "run-shell '$DIR/menu-sesh.sh'"
54	  "→ Agents"     A   "run-shell '$DIR/menu-agents.sh'"
55	  "→ Popups"     o   "run-shell '$DIR/menu-popups.sh'"
56	  "→ Theme"      T   "run-shell '$DIR/menu-theme.sh'"
57	  "→ System"     Y   "run-shell '$DIR/menu-system.sh'"
58	  ""             ""  ""
59	  "Cheatsheet"   "?" "display-popup -E -w 80% -h 80% -T ' tmux cheatsheet ' 'glow -p $DIR/cheatsheet.md 2>/dev/null || less $DIR/cheatsheet.md'"
60	  "Search keys"  "/" "run-shell -b ~/.tmux/plugins/tmux-fzf/scripts/keybinding.sh"
61	)
62	
63	rows=("${tier0[@]}")
64	if [ "$H" -ge 22 ]; then
65	  rows+=("${tier1[@]}" "${tier2[@]}")
66	elif [ "$H" -ge 14 ]; then
67	  rows+=("${tier2[@]}")
68	fi
69	
70	exec tmux display-menu -T "#[align=centre,bold]tmux (h=$H)" -x R -y P "${rows[@]}"
71
```
</details></tool-use>

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# Sesh picker — invoked from tmux popup menu (`prefix + Space` → "Sesh picker").
3	#
4	# Extracted from dot_config/tmux/keybindings.conf because the inline
5	# `display-menu` row tripped tmux's command parser: the fzf `{2..}` range
6	# syntax collides with tmux's `{ ... }` command-block delimiters, silently
7	# dropping the entire `display-menu` binding (no error, menu just doesn't
8	# open). See pitfalls/tmux-display-menu-silent-parse-failure.md.
9	#
10	# Run via:
11	#   bind-key -T prefix g run-shell '~/.config/tmux/sesh-picker.sh'
12	# or as a menu row:
13	#   "Sesh picker" g "run-shell '~/.config/tmux/sesh-picker.sh'"
14	
15	set -euo pipefail
16	
17	selected="$(
18	  sesh list --icons | fzf-tmux -p 80%,70% \
19	    --no-sort --ansi \
20	    --border-label ' sesh ' \
21	    --prompt '⚡  ' \
22	    --header '  ^a all ^t tmux ^g configs ^x zoxide ^d tmux kill ^f find' \
23	    --bind 'tab:down,btab:up' \
24	    --bind 'ctrl-a:change-prompt(⚡  )+reload(sesh list --icons)' \
25	    --bind 'ctrl-t:change-prompt(🪟  )+reload(sesh list -t --icons)' \
26	    --bind 'ctrl-g:change-prompt(⚙️  )+reload(sesh list -c --icons)' \
27	    --bind 'ctrl-x:change-prompt(📁  )+reload(sesh list -z --icons)' \
28	    --bind 'ctrl-f:change-prompt(🔎  )+reload(fd -H -d 2 -t d -E .Trash . ~)' \
29	    --bind 'ctrl-d:execute(tmux kill-session -t {2..})+change-prompt(⚡  )+reload(sesh list --icons)' \
30	    --preview-window 'right:55%' \
31	    --preview 'sesh preview {}'
32	)" || exit 0  # user pressed Esc
33	
34	[ -z "$selected" ] && exit 0
35	exec sesh connect "$selected"
36

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# upgrade_tools.sh — explicit, opt-in upgrade entrypoint.
3	#
4	# `chezmoi apply` is deliberately conservative (install-only, `state: present`,
5	# `creates:` idempotency). This script is the companion upgrade path: run it
6	# (or `just upgrade-*`) when you want to actually move tools forward.
7	#
8	# Design: each category is best-effort. A failure in one category does NOT
9	# abort later categories; a summary is printed at the end listing SUCCESS /
10	# FAILED / SKIPPED categories.
11	#
12	# Usage:
13	#   scripts/upgrade_tools.sh [all|<category> ...] [flags]
14	#
15	# Categories (also selectable via `all`):
16	#   externals brew mise uv npm cargo dotnet gem agents plugins
17	#
18	# Flags:
19	#   --dry-run          Print commands without executing.
20	#   --only a,b,c       Only run listed categories (comma-separated).
21	#   --skip a,b         Run everything except listed categories.
22	#   -h, --help         Show help.
23	#
24	# See docs/this_repo/upgrades.md and `## Upgrades` in AGENTS.md for rationale.
25	
26	set -u
27	# NOTE: we deliberately do not `set -e`. Each command is guarded by _run /
28	# run_category so we can continue past individual failures.
29	
30	# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
31	# Colors + loggers (match the style used in run_onchange_after_*.sh.tmpl)
32	# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
33	if [[ -t 1 ]]; then
34	  _C_RED='\033[0;31m'
35	  _C_GRN='\033[0;32m'
36	  _C_YLW='\033[1;33m'
37	  _C_BLU='\033[0;34m'
38	  _C_DIM='\033[2m'
39	  _C_RST='\033[0m'
40	else
41	  _C_RED='' _C_GRN='' _C_YLW='' _C_BLU='' _C_DIM='' _C_RST=''
42	fi
43	
44	info() { printf '%b\n' "${_C_BLU}[INFO]${_C_RST} $*"; }
45	success() { printf '%b\n' "${_C_GRN}[SUCCESS]${_C_RST} $*"; }
46	warn() { printf '%b\n' "${_C_YLW}[WARN]${_C_RST} $*"; }
47	error() { printf '%b\n' "${_C_RED}[ERROR]${_C_RST} $*" >&2; }
48	hr() { printf '%b\n' "${_C_DIM}────────────────────────────────────────────${_C_RST}"; }
49	
50	# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
51	# Source shared sudo helper (same file used by run_*.sh.tmpl via `include`)
52	# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
53	_REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
54	# shellcheck source=lib/sudo_shared.sh
55	if [[ -f "$_REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/sudo_shared.sh" ]]; then
56	  # shellcheck disable=SC1091
57	  source "$_REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/sudo_shared.sh"
58	fi
59	
60	# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
61	# Homebrew PATH detection (mirrors .chezmoiscripts/global/run_onchange_after_30_brew_bundle.sh.tmpl)
62	# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
63	setup_brew_path() {
64	  if command -v brew >/dev/null 2>&1; then
65	    return 0
66	  fi
67	  local candidates=(
68	    /opt/homebrew/bin/brew              # macOS Apple Silicon
69	    /usr/local/bin/brew                 # macOS Intel
70	    /home/linuxbrew/.linuxbrew/bin/brew # Linuxbrew system-wide
71	    "$HOME/.linuxbrew/bin/brew"         # Linuxbrew user
72	  )
73	  for b in "${candidates[@]}"; do
74	    if [[ -x "$b" ]]; then
75	      eval "$("$b" shellenv)"
76	      return 0
77	    fi
78	  done
79	  return 1
80	}
81	
82	# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
83	# Argument parsing
84	# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
85	DRY_RUN=0
86	ONLY=""
87	SKIP=""
88	SELECTED=()
89	
90	ALL_CATEGORIES=(externals brew mise uv npm cargo dotnet gem flatpak warp agents plugins)
91	
92	usage() {
93	  cat <<EOF
94	Usage: scripts/upgrade_tools.sh [all|<category> ...] [--dry-run] [--only a,b] [--skip a,b]
95	
96	Categories: ${ALL_CATEGORIES[*]}
97	
98	Run order for 'all': ${ALL_CATEGORIES[*]}
99	
100	Examples:
101	  scripts/upgrade_tools.sh                      # same as 'all'
102	  scripts/upgrade_tools.sh all
103	  scripts/upgrade_tools.sh brew uv
104	  scripts/upgrade_tools.sh --only brew,mise
105	  scripts/upgrade_tools.sh --skip agents,plugins
106	  scripts/upgrade_tools.sh --dry-run all
107	EOF
108	}
109	
110	while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
111	  case "$1" in
112	    -h | --help)
113	      usage
114	      exit 0
115	      ;;
116	    --dry-run)
117	      DRY_RUN=1
118	      shift
119	      ;;
120	    --only)
121	      ONLY="$2"
122	      shift 2
123	      ;;
124	    --only=*)
125	      ONLY="${1#--only=}"
126	      shift
127	      ;;
128	    --skip)
129	      SKIP="$2"
130	      shift 2
131	      ;;
132	    --skip=*)
133	      SKIP="${1#--skip=}"
134	      shift
135	      ;;
136	    all)
137	      SELECTED=("${ALL_CATEGORIES[@]}")
138	      shift
139	      ;;
140	    externals | brew | mise | uv | npm | cargo | dotnet | gem | flatpak | warp | agents | plugins)
141	      SELECTED+=("$1")
142	      shift
143	      ;;
144	    *)
145	      error "Unknown argument: $1"

148	      ;;
149	  esac
150	done

152	# No positional arg and no --only ⇒ default to 'all'
153	if [[ ${#SELECTED[@]} -eq 0 && -z "$ONLY" ]]; then
154	  SELECTED=("${ALL_CATEGORIES[@]}")
155	fi
156	
157	# --only overrides positional selection
158	if [[ -n "$ONLY" ]]; then
159	  IFS=',' read -ra SELECTED <<<"$ONLY"
160	fi
161	
162	# --skip filters the selection
163	if [[ -n "$SKIP" ]]; then
164	  IFS=',' read -ra _SKIP_ARR <<<"$SKIP"
165	  _FILTERED=()
166	  for c in "${SELECTED[@]}"; do
167	    local_skip=0
168	    for s in "${_SKIP_ARR[@]}"; do
169	      [[ "$c" == "$s" ]] && {
170	        local_skip=1
171	        break
172	      }
173	    done
174	    [[ "$local_skip" -eq 0 ]] && _FILTERED+=("$c")
175	  done
176	  SELECTED=("${_FILTERED[@]}")
177	fi
178	
179	# Validate every category exists
180	for c in "${SELECTED[@]}"; do
181	  ok=0
182	  for valid in "${ALL_CATEGORIES[@]}"; do
183	    [[ "$c" == "$valid" ]] && {
184	      ok=1
185	      break
186	    }
187	  done
188	  if [[ "$ok" -ne 1 ]]; then
189	    error "Unknown category: $c"
190	    usage
191	    exit 2
192	  fi
193	done
194	
195	# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
196	# Run helper: exec a command (or dry-run it), capture rc without aborting
197	# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
198	# Returns the rc of the invoked command (or 0 under --dry-run).
199	_run() {
200	  if [[ "$DRY_RUN" -eq 1 ]]; then
201	    printf '%b+ %s%b\n' "$_C_DIM" "$*" "$_C_RST"
202	    return 0
203	  fi
204	  printf '%b+ %s%b\n' "$_C_DIM" "$*" "$_C_RST"
205	  "$@"
206	}
207	
208	# _run_sh: same as _run but runs a single string through `bash -c`.
209	# Use for pipelines / redirections that _run cannot express.
210	_run_sh() {
211	  if [[ "$DRY_RUN" -eq 1 ]]; then
212	    printf '%b+ %s%b\n' "$_C_DIM" "$*" "$_C_RST"
213	    return 0
214	  fi
215	  printf '%b+ %s%b\n' "$_C_DIM" "$*" "$_C_RST"
216	  bash -c "$*"
217	}
218	
219	# run_category <name> <fn>: invoke fn, record success/fail, never abort.
220	SUCCESS_CATS=()
221	FAIL_CATS=()
222	SKIP_CATS=()
223	declare -A FAIL_REASONS
224	
225	run_category() {
226	  local name="$1" fn="$2"
227	  hr
228	  info "── category: ${name} ──"
229	  local rc=0
230	  # Disable errexit just in case someone later adds `set -e` at the top.
231	  set +e

243	    FAIL_CATS+=("$name")
244	    FAIL_REASONS[$name]="rc=$rc"
245	  fi
246	}
247	
248	# Convenience: category functions return 77 when prerequisites absent.
249	SKIP_RC=77
250	
251	# ============================================================================
252	# Category: externals — chezmoi self-upgrade + force externals refresh
253	# ============================================================================
254	cat_externals() {
255	  if ! command -v chezmoi >/dev/null 2>&1; then
256	    warn "chezmoi not found on PATH — skipping"

265	  if ! _run chezmoi upgrade; then

267	  fi

277	
278	# ============================================================================
279	# Category: brew — Homebrew formulas, casks (greedy), Brewfile, cleanup

281	cat_brew() {

304	            ;;

306	      else

308	      fi
309	    fi
310	  fi
311	
312	  local any_fail=0
313	  _run brew update || any_fail=1
314	  _run brew upgrade || any_fail=1
315	  # `--greedy` also upgrades casks that self-update (Electron apps etc.)
316	  _run brew upgrade --cask --greedy || any_fail=1
317	
318	  # Brewfile — call WITHOUT --no-upgrade so bundled items actually move.
319	  local brewdir="$HOME/.config/homebrew"
320	  if [[ -f "$brewdir/Brewfile" ]]; then
321	    _run brew bundle --file="$brewdir/Brewfile" || any_fail=1
322	  fi
323	  if [[ "$os" == "Darwin" && -f "$brewdir/Brewfile.darwin" ]]; then
324	    _run brew bundle --file="$brewdir/Brewfile.darwin" || any_fail=1
325	  elif [[ "$os" == "Linux" && -f "$brewdir/Brewfile.linux" ]]; then
326	    _run brew bundle --file="$brewdir/Brewfile.linux" || any_fail=1
327	  fi
328	
329	  _run brew cleanup || any_fail=1
330	
331	  return "$any_fail"
332	}

457	# Category: dotnet — upgrade each tool in dot_ansible/roles/dotnet_tools/defaults/main.yml
458	# ============================================================================
459	cat_dotnet() {
460	  # Resolve dotnet via mise shim first, then system PATH.
461	  local dotnet_cmd=""
462	  if [[ -x "$HOME/.local/share/mise/shims/dotnet" ]]; then
463	    dotnet_cmd="$HOME/.local/share/mise/shims/dotnet"
464	  elif command -v dotnet >/dev/null 2>&1; then
465	    dotnet_cmd="dotnet"
466	  else
467	    warn "dotnet not found — skipping"
468	    return $SKIP_RC
469	  fi
470	
471	  # Parse the tools list from defaults YAML. Small hand-rolled parser: we
472	  # only need lines of the form `  - name: <pkg>`. If parsing produces no
473	  # results, fall back to `dotnet tool list --global`.
474	  local defaults_file="$_REPO_ROOT/dot_ansible/roles/dotnet_tools/defaults/main.yml"
475	  local tools=()
476	  if [[ -f "$defaults_file" ]]; then
477	    while IFS= read -r line; do
478	      tools+=("$line")
479	    done < <(awk '
480	            /^dotnet_tools:/ { in_list=1; next }
481	            in_list && /^[^ ]/ { in_list=0 }
482	            in_list && /^[[:space:]]*-[[:space:]]*name:/ {
483	                sub(/^[[:space:]]*-[[:space:]]*name:[[:space:]]*/, "")
484	                gsub(/["'"'"']/, "")
485	                print
486	            }
487	        ' "$defaults_file")
488	  fi
489	
490	  if [[ ${#tools[@]} -eq 0 ]]; then
491	    info "Falling back to 'dotnet tool list --global'"
492	    if ! mapfile -t tools < <("$dotnet_cmd" tool list --global 2>/dev/null \
493	      | awk 'NR>2 && NF>0 {print $1}'); then
494	      warn "could not enumerate dotnet tools"
495	      return $SKIP_RC
496	    fi
497	  fi
498	
499	  if [[ ${#tools[@]} -eq 0 ]]; then
500	    warn "no dotnet tools to upgrade — skipping"
501	    return $SKIP_RC
502	  fi
503	
504	  # dotnet tools land under ~/.dotnet/tools.
505	  export PATH="$HOME/.dotnet/tools:$PATH"
506	
507	  local any_fail=0
508	  for t in "${tools[@]}"; do
509	    info "Upgrading dotnet tool: $t"
510	    _run "$dotnet_cmd" tool update --global "$t" || any_fail=1
511	  done
512	  return "$any_fail"
513	}

538	# Category: flatpak — `flatpak update` for user-scope Flathub apps
539	# ============================================================================
540	# We deliberately stick to user-scope (`--user`): no sudo required, and our
541	# ansible role installs everything via `method: user`. System-scope flatpaks
542	# need `sudo flatpak update --system`, which the user can run manually if
543	# they have any (rare in this repo's flow).
544	cat_flatpak() {
545	  if ! command -v flatpak >/dev/null 2>&1; then
546	    warn "flatpak not installed — skipping"
547	    return $SKIP_RC
548	  fi

550	  # Skip silently when there's nothing user-scoped to update — avoids logging
551	  # a "Nothing to do." into upgrade summaries on machines that have never set
552	  # discordChannel=flatpak.
553	  local n_user_apps
554	  n_user_apps="$(flatpak list --app --user 2>/dev/null | wc -l)"
555	  if [[ "$n_user_apps" -eq 0 ]]; then
556	    info "No user-scope Flatpak apps installed — skipping"
557	    return $SKIP_RC

566	# ============================================================================
567	# Category: warp — Linux apt-only upgrade for Warp Terminal
568	# ============================================================================
569	# macOS Warp is handled by `cat_brew` (cask "warp" + --greedy). On Linux,
570	# Warp's only supported channel is its own apt repo, but the in-app updater
571	# pastes `... && warp_finish_update <token>` into the prompt — that token is
572	# only valid inside a live Warp session and `warp_finish_update` is a
573	# Warp-injected shell function (not on PATH otherwise). So this category
574	# does the apt half only and leaves the user to restart Warp themselves.
575	#
576	# See docs/tools/warp.md for the full mechanism (token IPC handshake, etc.).
577	cat_warp() {
578	  if [[ "$(uname -s)" != "Linux" ]]; then
579	    info "Not Linux — Warp is upgraded via brew cask, skipping"
580	    return $SKIP_RC
581	  fi
582	  if ! command -v warp-terminal >/dev/null 2>&1; then
583	    warn "warp-terminal not installed — skipping"
584	    return $SKIP_RC
585	  fi
586	
587	  # warp-terminal is gated behind sudo apt. Reuse the shared sudo session so
588	  # the user isn't re-prompted across upgrade categories.
589	  if [[ "$DRY_RUN" -eq 0 ]] && declare -F sudo_session_init >/dev/null 2>&1; then
590	    if ! sudo_session_init "upgrade-warp"; then
591	      warn "Sudo session could not be established — skipping"
592	      return $SKIP_RC
593	    fi
594	    case "$(sudo_session_skip_reason)" in
595	      non-interactive | "")
596	        warn "Non-interactive mode without passwordless sudo — skipping warp"
597	        return $SKIP_RC
598	        ;;
599	    esac
600	  fi
601	
602	  local any_fail=0
603	  info "Refreshing Warp apt repo + installing only the warp-terminal candidate"
604	  # `apt update` covers all repos (cheap; usually run once per session anyway).
605	  _run sudo apt-get update || any_fail=1
606	  # `--only-upgrade` ensures we never accidentally re-install if the package
607	  # was uninstalled between commands; `-y` is safe because we're pinned to
608	  # one package name.
609	  _run sudo apt-get install --only-upgrade -y warp-terminal || any_fail=1
610	
611	  if [[ "$any_fail" -eq 0 ]]; then
612	    info "Warp on-disk binary updated. Quit + relaunch Warp to load the new version."
613	    info "(The in-app 'warp_finish_update <token>' graceful-restart only works from inside Warp.)"
614	  fi
615	  return "$any_fail"
616	}

618	# ============================================================================
619	# Category: agents — re-run install.sh for curl-installed CLI tools
620	# ============================================================================
621	# Only re-runs when the binary is already present. The installers are (by
622	# design) idempotent self-upgrades.
623	cat_agents() {
624	  local any_fail=0
625	  local ran_any=0
626	
627	  # Strategy: prefer the binary's built-in self-update subcommand (fast no-op
628	  # when already current; doesn't re-download the full binary). Fallback to
629	  # the official curl installer if the subcommand fails, hangs, or doesn't
630	  # exist. Inspection of upstream installers (2026-04) confirmed none of them
631	  # delegate to the self-update subcommand internally:
632	  #   - claude.sh   : always re-downloads, no version check
633	  #   - opencode.sh : has a same-version fast-path, but no `opencode upgrade`
634	  #   - cursor.sh   : always re-downloads, no version check
635	  #
636	  # We wrap the self-update call with a timeout (some `claude update` runs
637	  # have been observed hanging indefinitely on network checks) so a stuck
638	  # subcommand cannot block the whole upgrade flow.
639	  local _timeout_bin=""
640	  if command -v timeout >/dev/null 2>&1; then
641	    _timeout_bin="timeout"
642	  elif command -v gtimeout >/dev/null 2>&1; then
643	    _timeout_bin="gtimeout"
644	  fi
645	  _try_self_update_then_curl() {
646	    local label="$1" self_cmd="$2" curl_url="$3"
647	    info "Upgrading $label (trying self-update first)"
648	    local wrapped="$self_cmd"
649	    if [[ -n "$_timeout_bin" ]]; then
650	      wrapped="$_timeout_bin 90 $self_cmd"
651	    fi
652	    if _run_sh "$wrapped"; then
653	      return 0
654	    fi
655	    warn "$label self-update failed/timed out — falling back to official installer"
656	    local fallback="curl -fsSL $curl_url | bash"
657	    if [[ -n "$_timeout_bin" ]]; then
658	      fallback="$_timeout_bin 300 bash -c 'curl -fsSL $curl_url | bash'"
659	    fi
660	    _run_sh "$fallback"
661	  }
662	
663	  # Claude Code — `claude update` (alias: `claude upgrade`)
664	  if command -v claude >/dev/null 2>&1 \
665	    || [[ -x "$HOME/.claude/local/bin/claude" ]]; then
666	    _try_self_update_then_curl "Claude Code" \
667	      "claude update" \
668	      "https://claude.ai/install.sh" || any_fail=1
669	    ran_any=1
670	  fi
671	
672	  # OpenCode — `opencode upgrade`
673	  if command -v opencode >/dev/null 2>&1; then
674	    _try_self_update_then_curl "OpenCode" \
675	      "opencode upgrade" \
676	      "https://opencode.ai/install" || any_fail=1
677	    ran_any=1
678	  fi
679	
680	  # Cursor CLI — `cursor-agent update`
681	  if command -v cursor-agent >/dev/null 2>&1 \
682	    || command -v cursor-cli >/dev/null 2>&1 \
683	    || [[ -x "$HOME/.local/bin/cursor-agent" ]]; then
684	    _try_self_update_then_curl "Cursor CLI" \
685	      "cursor-agent update" \
686	      "https://cursor.com/install" || any_fail=1
687	    ran_any=1
688	  fi
689	
690	  # Ollama — Linux official installer (macOS is Homebrew-managed elsewhere).
691	  # No self-update subcommand exists.
692	  if [[ "$(uname -s)" == "Linux" ]] && command -v ollama >/dev/null 2>&1; then
693	    info "Upgrading Ollama (Linux installer)"
694	    _run_sh "curl -fsSL https://ollama.com/install.sh | sh" || any_fail=1
695	    ran_any=1
696	  fi
697	
698	  # llmfit — official local installer (Linux; macOS uses Homebrew)
699	  if [[ "$(uname -s)" == "Linux" ]] && command -v llmfit >/dev/null 2>&1; then
700	    info "Upgrading llmfit (Linux local installer)"
701	    _run_sh "curl -fsSL https://llmfit.axjns.dev/install.sh | sh -s -- --local" || any_fail=1
702	    ran_any=1
703	  fi
704	
705	  # RTK — official installer (no self-update subcommand)
706	  if command -v rtk >/dev/null 2>&1; then
707	    info "Upgrading RTK"
708	    _run_sh "curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rtk-ai/rtk/refs/heads/master/install.sh | sh" || any_fail=1
709	    ran_any=1
710	  fi
711	
712	  # SpecStory — brew tap when available (macOS), else GitHub release script.
713	  # The installer script is idempotent and pulls latest by default, so re-running
714	  # it is the upgrade path on Linux (and on macOS when not brew-managed).
715	  if command -v specstory >/dev/null 2>&1 \
716	    || [[ -x "$HOME/.local/bin/specstory" ]]; then
717	    local specstory_handled=0
718	    if [[ "$(uname -s)" == "Darwin" ]] && setup_brew_path \
719	      && brew list --formula specstoryai/tap/specstory >/dev/null 2>&1; then
720	      info "Upgrading SpecStory via Homebrew tap"
721	      _run brew upgrade specstoryai/tap/specstory || any_fail=1
722	      specstory_handled=1
723	    fi
724	    if [[ "$specstory_handled" -eq 0 ]]; then
725	      if [[ -x "$_REPO_ROOT/scripts/install_specstory.sh" ]]; then
726	        info "Upgrading SpecStory via install_specstory.sh (latest GitHub release)"
727	        _run "$_REPO_ROOT/scripts/install_specstory.sh" || any_fail=1
728	      else
729	        warn "specstory present but install_specstory.sh not found — skipping"
730	      fi
731	    fi
732	    ran_any=1
733	  fi
734	
735	  if [[ "$ran_any" -eq 0 ]]; then
736	    warn "no known curl-installed agents detected — skipping"
737	    return $SKIP_RC
738	  fi
739	
740	  return "$any_fail"
741	}

743	# ============================================================================
744	# Category: plugins — editor/tmux/pre-commit/tldr/gh plugin upgrades
745	# ============================================================================
746	cat_plugins() {
747	  local any_fail=0
748	  local ran_any=0
749	  local claude_hud_helper="$_REPO_ROOT/dot_ansible/roles/coding_agents/files/claude_hud_sync.py"
750	  local claude_hud_installed=0
751	
752	  # LazyVim (Neovim plugins)

754	    info "Syncing LazyVim plugins (nvim --headless +Lazy! sync +qa)"

762	    info "Updating tmux plugins via TPM"

765	  fi
766	
767	  # claude-hud plugin cache / installed_plugins.json
768	  if [[ -d "$HOME/.claude/plugins/cache/claude-hud" ]]; then
769	    claude_hud_installed=1
770	  elif [[ -f "$HOME/.claude/plugins/installed_plugins.json" ]] \
771	    && grep -q '"claude-hud@claude-hud"' "$HOME/.claude/plugins/installed_plugins.json"; then
772	    claude_hud_installed=1
773	  fi
774	  if [[ "$claude_hud_installed" -eq 1 ]] \
775	    && command -v python3 >/dev/null 2>&1 \
776	    && [[ -f "$claude_hud_helper" ]]; then
777	    info "Refreshing claude-hud plugin"
778	    _run python3 "$claude_hud_helper" --only-if-installed || any_fail=1
779	    ran_any=1
780	  fi
781	
782	  # pre-commit autoupdate — only when we're in the dotfiles repo itself
783	  if command -v pre-commit >/dev/null 2>&1 \
784	    && [[ -f "$_REPO_ROOT/.pre-commit-config.yaml" ]]; then
785	    info "Running pre-commit autoupdate on the dotfiles repo"
786	    (cd "$_REPO_ROOT" && _run pre-commit autoupdate) || any_fail=1
787	    ran_any=1
788	  fi
789	
790	  # tldr cache
791	  if command -v tldr >/dev/null 2>&1; then
792	    info "Updating tldr cache"
793	    _run tldr --update || any_fail=1
794	    ran_any=1
795	  fi
796	
797	  # gh extensions
798	  if command -v gh >/dev/null 2>&1; then
799	    info "Upgrading gh extensions"
800	    _run gh extension upgrade --all || any_fail=1
801	    ran_any=1
802	  fi
803	
804	  if [[ "$ran_any" -eq 0 ]]; then
805	    warn "no plugin managers detected — skipping"
806	    return $SKIP_RC
807	  fi
808	  return "$any_fail"
809	}
810	
811	# ============================================================================
812	# Main: dispatch selected categories in defined order
813	# ============================================================================
814	hr
815	if [[ "$DRY_RUN" -eq 1 ]]; then
816	  info "upgrade_tools.sh — categories: ${SELECTED[*]} (dry-run)"
817	else
818	  info "upgrade_tools.sh — categories: ${SELECTED[*]}"
819	fi
820	if [[ "$DRY_RUN" -eq 1 ]]; then
821	  warn "DRY-RUN MODE — commands are printed, not executed"
822	fi
823	
824	# Run in the canonical ALL_CATEGORIES order (regardless of CLI arg order).
825	for cat in "${ALL_CATEGORIES[@]}"; do
826	  for sel in "${SELECTED[@]}"; do
827	    if [[ "$cat" == "$sel" ]]; then
828	      case "$cat" in
829	        externals) run_category externals cat_externals ;;
830	        brew) run_category brew cat_brew ;;
831	        mise) run_category mise cat_mise ;;
832	        uv) run_category uv cat_uv ;;
833	        npm) run_category npm cat_npm ;;
834	        cargo) run_category cargo cat_cargo ;;
835	        dotnet) run_category dotnet cat_dotnet ;;
836	        gem) run_category gem cat_gem ;;
837	        flatpak) run_category flatpak cat_flatpak ;;
838	        warp) run_category warp cat_warp ;;
839	        agents) run_category agents cat_agents ;;
840	        plugins) run_category plugins cat_plugins ;;
841	      esac
842	      break
843	    fi
844	  done
845	done
846	
847	# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
848	# Summary
849	# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
850	hr
851	info "Upgrade Summary"
852	if [[ ${#SUCCESS_CATS[@]} -gt 0 ]]; then
853	  success "OK:      ${SUCCESS_CATS[*]}"
854	fi
855	if [[ ${#SKIP_CATS[@]} -gt 0 ]]; then
856	  warn "SKIPPED: ${SKIP_CATS[*]} (prerequisite missing)"
857	fi
858	if [[ ${#FAIL_CATS[@]} -gt 0 ]]; then
859	  error "FAILED:  ${FAIL_CATS[*]}"
860	  for c in "${FAIL_CATS[@]}"; do
861	    error "   - ${c}: ${FAIL_REASONS[$c]:-unknown}"
862	  done
863	  exit 1
864	fi
865	exit 0

52	# Chezmoi
53	# ============================================================================
54	#
55	# All `chezmoi-*` recipes pass `--no-pager` so output streams straight to
56	# stdout instead of spawning the configured pager (delta in this repo).
57	# Critical for non-interactive callers (CI, coding agents, `just` itself
58	# in scripted contexts) — without it, delta tries to alternate-screen
59	# / line-buffer over a pipe and either panics, hangs, or eats output.
60	# Use raw `chezmoi diff` directly when you want the interactive pager.
61	
62	# Show what would change
63	chezmoi-diff:
64	    chezmoi --no-pager diff
65	
66	# Apply dotfiles
67	chezmoi-apply:
68	    chezmoi --no-pager apply
69	
70	# Dry run (preview without applying)
71	chezmoi-dry-run:
72	    chezmoi --no-pager apply --dry-run
73	
74	# Show chezmoi status
75	chezmoi-status:
76	    chezmoi --no-pager status
77	
78	# Re-initialize chezmoi (for testing prompts)
79	chezmoi-reinit:
80	    chezmoi init
81	
82	# Run the interactive bootstrap wrapper from the LOCAL chezmoi source.
83	# Use this instead of `curl|bash` when you're on a slow / GFW-throttled network
84	# and have already cloned the repo. Skips the bootstrap.sh stage entirely:
85	# uv resolves PEP 723 deps locally; chezmoi init clones from the same remote
86	# you're cloned from. Pass extra args after `--`:
87	#     just bootstrap-local                  # interactive
88	#     just bootstrap-local -- doctor        # schema parity check
89	#     just bootstrap-local -- list-bundles  # show bundles
90	#     just bootstrap-local -- --yes --bundle minimal  # non-interactive
91	bootstrap-local *ARGS:
92	    @echo "[bootstrap-local] running scripts/init/dotfiles_init.py from local source"
93	    uv run --script scripts/init/dotfiles_init.py {{ARGS}}
94	
95	# Verbose bootstrap-local: shows uv resolver output (download/build steps).
96	bootstrap-local-verbose *ARGS:
97	    @echo "[bootstrap-local-verbose] uv --verbose; expect lots of resolver output"
98	    uv run --verbose --script scripts/init/dotfiles_init.py {{ARGS}}
99	
100	# Clear run_once script state (allows re-running run_once scripts)
101	chezmoi-clear-scripts:
102	    chezmoi state delete-bucket --bucket=scriptState
103	
104	# Clear script state and re-apply (for testing run_once scripts)
105	chezmoi-rerun-scripts:
106	    chezmoi state delete-bucket --bucket=scriptState
107	    chezmoi --no-pager apply -v

109	# ============================================================================
110	# Dotfiles backup (~/.dotfiles_backup)
111	# ============================================================================
112	#
113	# Pre-apply snapshots produced by `run_before_01_backup_dotfiles.sh.tmpl`.
114	# `backupMode` ∈ {smart (default), full, off}; smart only captures files
115	# `chezmoi apply` would overwrite/delete (per `chezmoi status` col 2 = M/D).
116	
117	# List backup snapshots with file count
118	list-backups:
119	    @if [ ! -d "$HOME/.dotfiles_backup" ]; then echo "No backups in ~/.dotfiles_backup"; exit 0; fi
120	    @for d in "$HOME"/.dotfiles_backup/*/; do \
121	        [ -d "$d" ] || continue; \
122	        ts=$(basename "$d"); \
123	        n=$(find "$d" -type f 2>/dev/null | wc -l | tr -d ' '); \
124	        printf '%s  (%s file(s))\n' "$ts" "$n"; \
125	    done
126	
127	# Diff a backup snapshot against current files in ~ (read-only inspection)
128	diff-backup ts:
129	    @snap="$HOME/.dotfiles_backup/{{ts}}"; \
130	    if [ ! -d "$snap" ]; then echo "No such backup: {{ts}}" >&2; exit 1; fi; \
131	    find "$snap" -type f | while read -r backed; do \
132	        rel="${backed#$snap/}"; live="$HOME/$rel"; \
133	        if [ ! -e "$live" ]; then \
134	            printf '\n=== %s: in backup, missing from live ===\n' "$rel"; \
135	        elif ! cmp -s "$backed" "$live"; then \
136	            printf '\n=== %s ===\n' "$rel"; \
137	            diff -u "$backed" "$live" || true; \
138	        fi; \
139	    done

179	# Install pre-commit via uv (pinned to Python 3.13 — same command as the
180	# security_tools ansible role, so both paths converge on ~/.local/bin/pre-commit).
181	# Avoids the macOS Homebrew python@3.14 pyexpat ABI mismatch that breaks hook
182	# virtualenv creation. Run `just pre-commit-doctor` if hooks start failing.
183	pre-commit-install-tool:
184	    #!/usr/bin/env bash
185	    set -euo pipefail
186	    if ! command -v uv &>/dev/null; then
187	        echo "Error: uv not found on PATH. Run chezmoi bootstrap first (installs uv into ~/.local/bin), or install uv manually from https://astral.sh/uv." >&2
188	        exit 1
189	    fi
190	    uv tool install --force pre-commit --python 3.13
191	    echo "pre-commit installed: $(pre-commit --version) @ $(command -v pre-commit)"

394	# ============================================================================
395	# Fleet (multi-host chezmoi apply)
396	# ============================================================================
397	# Run `chezmoi update --init` (or apply / diff) across many remote hosts in
398	# parallel. Inventory: ~/.config/fleet/machines.toml (seeded by chezmoi as a
399	# `create_private_` template — your edits are preserved). Sudo password
400	# sources: plain / interactive prompt / Bitwarden CLI / none.
401	# Per-host log: logs/fleet-apply/<UTC-timestamp>/<host>.log
402	# Exit code = number of failed hosts.
403	# See docs/this_repo/fleet-apply.md for full schema and troubleshooting.
404	
405	# Apply chezmoi update to all configured hosts in parallel
406	fleet-apply *ARGS:
407	    ./scripts/fleet_apply.py {{ARGS}}
408	
409	# Preview only: runs `chezmoi diff` on every host (no changes applied)
410	fleet-apply-dry-run *ARGS:
411	    ./scripts/fleet_apply.py --dry-run {{ARGS}}
412	
413	# Quick `chezmoi diff` against ONE host (serial, debug-friendly output).
414	# Use this in vibe loops to see exactly what your latest commit will do
415	# on a specific machine before pushing/applying for real.
416	fleet-diff HOST *ARGS:
417	    ./scripts/fleet_apply.py --dry-run --hosts {{HOST}} --serial {{ARGS}}
418	
419	# Apply ONLY a single chezmoi target on each host (skips ansible / Brewfile).
420	# PATH is the chezmoi target path, e.g. `.config/zsh/aliases.zsh` or
421	# `.zshrc`. Fast feedback for editing one dotfile across the fleet without
422	# waiting for full Linuxbrew/ansible cycles. Pass extra `--hosts HOST` to
423	# scope. Internally sets CHEZMOI_FLEET_APPLY_PATH so the wrapper runs
424	# `chezmoi apply <relpath>` instead of `chezmoi update --init`.
425	fleet-apply-file PATH *ARGS:
426	    ./scripts/fleet_apply.py --apply-only-path {{PATH}} {{ARGS}}
427	
428	# Apply a feature BRANCH instead of pulling main. Each remote does
429	# `git fetch origin BRANCH && git checkout -B BRANCH origin/BRANCH &&
430	# git merge --ff-only origin/BRANCH` before chezmoi apply. Fails loud
431	# on divergence — use `just fleet-apply-branch-force` to nuke local
432	# state with `git reset --hard`. Local hosts skip this entirely (source
433	# is your editor's working tree).
434	fleet-apply-branch BRANCH *ARGS:
435	    ./scripts/fleet_apply.py --branch {{BRANCH}} {{ARGS}}
436	
437	# Like fleet-apply-branch but uses `git reset --hard origin/BRANCH` on
438	# remotes, destroying any local divergence. Use after force-pushing a
439	# rebased topic branch so every host follows.
440	fleet-apply-branch-force BRANCH *ARGS:
441	    ./scripts/fleet_apply.py --branch {{BRANCH}} --force-checkout {{ARGS}}
442	
443	# Apply to a single named host in --serial mode (debug-friendly output)
444	fleet-apply-one HOST *ARGS:
445	    ./scripts/fleet_apply.py --hosts {{HOST}} --serial {{ARGS}}
446	
447	# Kill orphan chezmoi/ansible processes on every host (cleanup after Ctrl+C)
448	fleet-apply-kill *ARGS:
449	    ./scripts/fleet_apply.py --kill-orphans {{ARGS}}
450	
451	# Probe each host for running chezmoi/ansible (use after killing local SSH)
452	fleet-apply-status *ARGS:
453	    ./scripts/fleet_apply.py --status {{ARGS}}
454	
455	# Like fleet-apply-status but re-poll every Ns until everyone is idle
456	# (Ctrl+C to stop). Default interval 10s; override with --watch=N in ARGS.
457	fleet-apply-watch *ARGS:
458	    ./scripts/fleet_apply.py --status --watch 10 {{ARGS}}
459	
460	# Live-tail the remote fleet-apply log of HOST (defaults to most recent run);
461	# pass `HOST:RUN_ID` (e.g. lab-box:20260422T133615Z) to pin a specific run.
462	# Ctrl+C stops the viewer only — the remote run keeps going.
463	fleet-apply-tail HOST *ARGS:
464	    ./scripts/fleet_apply.py --tail {{HOST}} {{ARGS}}
465	
466	# Compact post-mortem summary across the fleet: final task reached, ansible
467	# runtime, top slow tasks, failed run_* script, exit code. Defaults to each
468	# host's latest run; pin to one run with --compact-run-id RUN_ID in ARGS.
469	fleet-apply-compact *ARGS:
470	    ./scripts/fleet_apply.py --compact {{ARGS}}

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# Layout submenu (invoked from menu.sh / prefix + Enter popup).
3	#
4	# Note: this script is intentionally NOT wired into the right-click window
5	# menu. Nested display-menu via `run-shell` from a mouse-driven parent has
6	# unreliable mouse-event behaviour (selection silently does nothing on
7	# second invocation). The right-click window menu inlines layouts directly.
8	# See pitfalls/tmux-submenu-flash-and-bottom-right.md for the full story.
9	set -euo pipefail
10	exec tmux display-menu -T " Layouts " -x R -y P \
11	  "Even horizontal" 1 "select-layout even-horizontal" \
12	  "Even vertical"   2 "select-layout even-vertical" \
13	  "Main horizontal" 3 "select-layout main-horizontal" \
14	  "Main vertical"   4 "select-layout main-vertical" \
15	  "Tiled (grid)"    5 "select-layout tiled" \
16	  "Resize 75%"      "+" "resize-pane -x 75%" \
17	  "" "" "" \
18	  "Pane left"       h "select-pane -L" \
19	  "Pane down"       j "select-pane -D" \
20	  "Pane up"         k "select-pane -U" \
21	  "Pane right"      l "select-pane -R" \
22	  "" "" "" \
23	  "Swap left/up"    "{" "swap-pane -U" \
24	  "Swap right/down" "}" "swap-pane -D"

```text
1	# 11_tools_picker.zsh - Interactive CLI tools picker (fzf ZLE widget)
2	# Reads ~/.config/docs/tools/cli-tools.md for the tool list (deployed by chezmoi).
3	#
4	# Alt+T  →  open picker
5	#   Enter      paste invocation to shell buffer (you still press Enter to run)
6	#   Ctrl+E     execute the tool directly (good for TUI apps: btop, lazygit, etc.)
7	#   Ctrl+/     toggle preview panel (shows tldr or --help)
8	#
9	# The invocation for tools that need arguments has a trailing space,
10	# so pressing Enter pastes e.g. "rg " — cursor lands after the space,
11	# ready for you to type your arguments.
12	
13	_TOOLS_DOC="${HOME}/.config/docs/tools/cli-tools.md"
14	
15	# Bail silently if the data file hasn't been deployed yet or fzf is missing
16	[[ -f "$_TOOLS_DOC" ]] || return 0
17	command -v fzf &>/dev/null || return 0
18	
19	# Parse the markdown tables into "INVOCATION<TAB>DESCRIPTION" lines.
20	# Tab separator preserves the trailing space in invocations like "rg ".
21	_tools_list() {
22	    awk -F'|' '/^[[:space:]]*\|[[:space:]]*`/ {
23	      inv=$3; sub(/^[[:space:]]*`/,"",inv); sub(/`[[:space:]]*$/,"",inv)
24	      desc=$4; sub(/^[[:space:]]*/,"",desc); sub(/[[:space:]]*$/,"",desc)
25	      printf "%s\t%s\n", inv, desc
26	    }' "$_TOOLS_DOC"
27	}
28	
29	# ZLE widget: opens fzf picker, pastes selected invocation to the shell command line.
30	tools-picker() {
31	    {
32	        exec </dev/tty
33	        exec <&1
34	
35	        local selected
36	        selected=$(
37	            _tools_list | fzf \
38	                --ansi \
39	                --border \
40	                --prompt ' tools  ' \
41	                --header 'Enter: paste  Ctrl+E: execute  Ctrl+/: preview' \
42	                --delimiter=$'\t' \
43	                --with-nth=1,2 \
44	                --preview 'tool=$(printf "%s" {1} | awk "{print \$1}" | sed "s/ *$//"); (command -v tldr >/dev/null 2>&1 && tldr "$tool" 2>/dev/null) || "$tool" --help 2>&1 | head -50' \
45	                --preview-window='right:55%:wrap:hidden' \
46	                --bind='ctrl-/:toggle-preview' \
47	                --bind='ctrl-e:execute(eval $(printf "%s" {1} | awk "{print \$1}"))+abort'
48	        )
49	
50	        zle reset-prompt >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
51	        [[ -z "$selected" ]] && return
52	
53	        # Extract the invocation (field 1 before the tab), preserving trailing space
54	        local invocation
55	        invocation=$(printf '%s' "$selected" | cut -f1)
56	
57	        # Paste to shell command line buffer without executing
58	        LBUFFER="${LBUFFER}${invocation}"
59	        zle redisplay
60	    }
61	}
62	
63	zle -N tools-picker
64	
65	# Alt+T (mnemonic: Tools)
66	# Alt+S = sesh-sessions, Alt+C = fzf cd — Alt+T is free
67	bindkey -M emacs '\et' tools-picker
68	bindkey -M viins '\et' tools-picker
69	bindkey -M vicmd '\et' tools-picker
70
```
</details></tool-use>

```text
1	# 12_television.zsh - Television (tv) shell integration
2	#
3	# Tab completion via ~/.zfunc/_tv (regenerated on version change).
4	# We do NOT use `tv init zsh` because it binds Ctrl+T and Ctrl+R,
5	# which conflict with fzf's shell integration.
6	#
7	# Instead, tv channels are bound to Alt keys:
8	#   Alt+R  tv shell history     (tv-style history search)
9	#   Alt+P  tv files             (tv-style file/path picker)
10	#   Alt+G  tv git-log           (git log browser)
11	#   Alt+E  tv env               (environment variables)
12	#   Alt+A  tv aliases           (all aliases & functions)
13	#   Alt+I  tv git-ops           (insert git command from VSCode/GitLens menu)
14	#
15	# fzf keeps Ctrl+T / Ctrl+R / Alt+C (muscle memory).
16	# tv gets Alt namespace for advanced pickers.
17	#
18	# Aliases cache: ~/.cache/tv/aliases.txt is generated on shell startup
19	# so that `tv aliases` channel can read it without spawning `zsh -ic`
20	# (which causes tty suspend issues).
21	#
22	# See: https://github.com/alexpasmantier/television
23	
24	command -v tv &>/dev/null || return 0
25	
26	# --- Tab completion (written to ~/.zfunc/, picked up by compinit) ---
27	if [[ -d ~/.zfunc ]]; then
28	  local _tv_ver="$(tv --version 2>/dev/null)"
29	  if [[ ! -f ~/.zfunc/_tv ]] || ! grep -q "${_tv_ver}" ~/.zfunc/_tv 2>/dev/null; then
30	    tv completions zsh > ~/.zfunc/_tv 2>/dev/null
31	  fi
32	fi
33	
34	# --- Generate aliases cache for tv aliases channel ---
35	{
36	  mkdir -p ~/.cache/tv
37	  {
38	    alias | while IFS="=" read -r name rest; do
39	      printf "%-22s  alias   %s\n" "$name" "$rest"
40	    done
41	    typeset -f + | while read -r name; do
42	      printf "%-22s  func\n" "$name"
43	    done
44	  } | sort > ~/.cache/tv/aliases.txt
45	} &>/dev/null &!
46	
47	# --- Custom ZLE widgets for tv channels ---
48	
49	_tv_channel_widget() {
50	  emulate -L zsh
51	  zle -I
52	  local output
53	  output=$(tv "$1" --no-status-bar --inline < /dev/tty)
54	  zle reset-prompt
55	  if [[ -n $output ]]; then
56	    LBUFFER+="$output"
57	  fi
58	}
59	
60	_tv_history() {
61	  emulate -L zsh
62	  zle -I
63	  local output current_prompt
64	  current_prompt=$LBUFFER
65	  output=$(history -n -1 0 | tv --no-status-bar --input "$current_prompt" --inline < /dev/tty)
66	  zle reset-prompt
67	  if [[ -n $output ]]; then
68	    RBUFFER=""
69	    LBUFFER="$output"
70	  fi
71	}
72	
73	_tv_files()   { _tv_channel_widget "files"; }
74	_tv_gitlog()  { _tv_channel_widget "git-log"; }
75	_tv_env()     { _tv_channel_widget "env"; }
76	_tv_aliases() { _tv_channel_widget "aliases"; }
77	_tv_gitops()  { _tv_channel_widget "git-ops"; }
78	
79	zle -N tv-history  _tv_history
80	zle -N tv-files    _tv_files
81	zle -N tv-gitlog   _tv_gitlog
82	zle -N tv-env      _tv_env
83	zle -N tv-aliases  _tv_aliases
84	zle -N tv-gitops   _tv_gitops
85	
86	# --- Keybindings (Alt namespace) ---
87	# Note: Alt+F is reserved for forward-word (emacs mode default).
88	bindkey '\er' tv-history   # Alt+R
89	bindkey '\ep' tv-files     # Alt+P (path/pick)
90	bindkey '\eg' tv-gitlog    # Alt+G
91	bindkey '\ee' tv-env       # Alt+E
92	bindkey '\ea' tv-aliases   # Alt+A
93	bindkey '\ei' tv-gitops    # Alt+I (insert git op)
94
```

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# Session/window management submenu
3	set -euo pipefail
4	exec tmux display-menu -T " Session mgmt " -x R -y P \
5	  "Rename session"     "\$" "command-prompt -I '#S' 'rename-session -- \"%%\"'" \
6	  "Rename window"      ","  "command-prompt -I '#W' 'rename-window -- \"%%\"'" \
7	  "" "" "" \
8	  "New session"        N  "command-prompt -p 'New session:' 'new-session -s \"%%\"'" \
9	  "Move window to"     m  "command-prompt -p 'Move window to (session[:index]):' 'move-window -t \"%%\"'" \
10	  "Break pane to"      r  "command-prompt -p 'Break pane to (session[:index]):' 'break-pane -t \"%%\"'" \
11	  "Link window to"     K  "command-prompt -p 'Link window to (session[:index]):' 'link-window -t \"%%\"'" \
12	  "Renumber windows"   R  "run-shell 'tmux move-window -r && tmux display-message \"Windows renumbered\"'" \
13	  "" "" "" \
14	  "Join marked here (h)" j "join-pane -h" \
15	  "Join marked here (v)" J "join-pane -v" \
16	  "Send pane to..."    s  "choose-tree -Zw -F '#{window_name}' \"join-pane -h -s '#{pane_id}' -t '%%' ; display-message 'Sent pane to target'\"" \
17	  "" "" "" \
18	  "Kill pane"          x  "confirm-before -p 'Kill pane? (y/n)' kill-pane" \
19	  "Kill window"        W  "confirm-before -p 'Kill window #W? (y/n)' kill-window" \
20	  "Kill session"       X  "confirm-before -p 'Kill session #S? (y/n)' kill-session" \
21	  "Kill session & exit" E  "confirm-before -p 'Kill session #S and exit tmux? (y/n)' \"run-shell '$HOME/.config/tmux/kill-session-exit.sh'\"" \
22	  "Kill all sessions"  Q  "confirm-before -p 'Kill ALL sessions (tmux server)? (y/n)' kill-server"
23

1	#!/bin/bash
2	# Run brew bundle when Brewfiles change
3	# Runs when general Brew apps are enabled, or on macOS when AI desktop apps are enabled
4	# Profile: {{ .profile }}
5	# installBrewApps: {{ .installBrewApps }}
6	# installAiDesktopApps: {{ .installAiDesktopApps }}
7	
8	{{ if and (not .installBrewApps) (or (ne .chezmoi.os "darwin") (not .installAiDesktopApps)) -}}
9	# Brew app installation is disabled for this profile
10	# To enable, run: chezmoi init --force
11	exit 0
12	{{ end -}}
13	
14	{{ if eq .chezmoi.os "darwin" -}}
15	# === Brewfile Hashes (changes trigger re-run) ===
16	# Brewfile: {{ include "dot_config/homebrew/Brewfile.tmpl" | sha256sum }}
17	# Brewfile.darwin: {{ include "dot_config/homebrew/Brewfile.darwin.tmpl" | sha256sum }}
18	{{ else -}}
19	# === Brewfile Hashes (changes trigger re-run) ===
20	# Brewfile: {{ include "dot_config/homebrew/Brewfile.tmpl" | sha256sum }}
21	# Brewfile.linux: {{ include "dot_config/homebrew/Brewfile.linux.tmpl" | sha256sum }}
22	{{ end -}}
23	
24	set -e
25	
26	# Colors
27	RED='\033[0;31m'
28	GREEN='\033[0;32m'
29	YELLOW='\033[1;33m'
30	BLUE='\033[0;34m'
31	NC='\033[0m'
32	
33	info() { echo -e "${BLUE}[INFO]${NC} $1"; }
34	success() { echo -e "${GREEN}[SUCCESS]${NC} $1"; }
35	warn() { echo -e "${YELLOW}[WARN]${NC} $1"; }
36	error() { echo -e "${RED}[ERROR]${NC} $1"; }
37	
38	# Setup Homebrew PATH
39	{{ if eq .chezmoi.os "darwin" -}}
40	if [[ -f /opt/homebrew/bin/brew ]]; then
41	    eval "$(/opt/homebrew/bin/brew shellenv)"
42	elif [[ -f /usr/local/bin/brew ]]; then
43	    eval "$(/usr/local/bin/brew shellenv)"
44	fi
45	{{ else -}}
46	# Linuxbrew
47	if [[ -d /home/linuxbrew/.linuxbrew ]]; then
48	    eval "$(/home/linuxbrew/.linuxbrew/bin/brew shellenv)"
49	elif [[ -d "$HOME/.linuxbrew" ]]; then
50	    eval "$("$HOME/.linuxbrew/bin/brew" shellenv)"
51	fi
52	{{ end -}}
53	
54	# Check if brew is available
55	if ! command -v brew &> /dev/null; then
56	    {{ if eq .chezmoi.os "darwin" -}}
57	    error "Homebrew not found. It should have been installed by bootstrap."
58	    exit 1
59	    {{ else -}}
60	    warn "Homebrew (Linuxbrew) not installed. Skipping brew bundle."
61	    warn "To install: /bin/bash -c \"\$(curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Homebrew/install/HEAD/install.sh)\""
62	    exit 0
63	    {{ end -}}
64	fi
65	
66	BREWFILE_DIR="$HOME/.config/homebrew"
67	
68	# Check if Brewfiles exist
69	if [[ ! -f "$BREWFILE_DIR/Brewfile" ]]; then
70	    warn "Brewfile not found at $BREWFILE_DIR/Brewfile"
71	    warn "Run 'chezmoi apply' to deploy Brewfiles first."
72	    exit 0
73	fi
74	
75	{{ if eq .chezmoi.os "darwin" -}}
76	# --- Shared sudo session (see scripts/lib/sudo_shared.sh)
77	# Inlined at render time. By the time brew-bundle runs, bootstrap and ansible
78	# will usually have already prompted + spawned the watchdog (which keeps the
79	# TTY timestamp warm every 50 s). `sudo_session_init` is idempotent: if the
80	# session already exists, it just re-exports env vars + re-registers traps.
81	# If the user invoked brew-bundle standalone (without the other phases), the
82	# prompt happens here instead.
83	{{ include "scripts/lib/sudo_shared.sh" }}
84	# --- end sudo helper
85	
86	# Pre-authenticate sudo so Homebrew cask pkg installers (e.g. google-drive,
87	# squirrel, ollama-app) can invoke /usr/sbin/installer without prompting from
88	# a non-TTY child. The watchdog refreshes the timestamp every 50 s, which
89	# is well inside sudo's default 5-minute tty_tickets window.
90	if sudo_session_init "brew"; then
91	    case "$(sudo_session_skip_reason)" in
92	        cached)
93	            # Warm the current TTY's timestamp right now so the FIRST cask
94	            # that shells out to `sudo /usr/sbin/installer` finds a live
95	            # ticket (cask installers read a TTY timestamp, not stdin).
96	            sudo_session_warm_cache || warn "sudo_session_warm_cache failed; pkg casks may prompt or fail"
97	            ;;
98	        passwordless)
99	            info "Passwordless sudo detected"
100	            ;;
