2	
3	This repo manages the *global* config files of three coding-agent CLIs via chezmoi `modify_` overlays:
4	
5	| CLI | Live file | Source script | Merge engine |
6	|---|---|---|---|
7	| Cursor | `~/.cursor/cli-config.json` | [`dot_cursor/modify_cli-config.json.tmpl`](../../dot_cursor/modify_cli-config.json.tmpl) | `jq '. * $overlay'` |
8	| OpenCode (server/runtime) | `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json` | [`dot_config/opencode/modify_opencode.json.tmpl`](../../dot_config/opencode/modify_opencode.json.tmpl) | `jq '. * $overlay'` |
9	| OpenCode (TUI) | `~/.config/opencode/tui.json` | [`dot_config/opencode/modify_tui.json.tmpl`](../../dot_config/opencode/modify_tui.json.tmpl) | `jq '. * $overlay'` |
10	| Codex | `~/.codex/config.toml` | [`dot_codex/modify_config.toml.tmpl`](../../dot_codex/modify_config.toml.tmpl) | Python `tomllib` + inline emitter |
11	
12	Overlay payloads live under [`.chezmoitemplates/agents/`](../../.chezmoitemplates/agents/) and are sourced via `{{ template ... }}` includes so the merge logic can be tested independently of overlay contents.
13	
14	## Why `modify_` and not full file management
15	
16	All three CLIs **rewrite their config file at runtime** to record machine-local state: auth tokens, telemetry IDs, per-project trust grants, marketplace registrations with absolute paths, plugin-cache hashes, last-used provider hints, etc. Tracking the whole file as managed content would:
17	
18	1. Leak secrets (`authInfo`, `auth.json` content) into the dotfiles repo.
19	2. Bake one machine's absolute paths (`/Users/me/.codex/.tmp/...`) into another machine's apply.
20	3. Produce constant `chezmoi diff` noise as the CLI churns the file.
21	
22	The `modify_` overlay model deep-merges only the keys we explicitly enforce; everything else passes through verbatim.
23	
24	## What each overlay enforces
25	
26	### Cursor — [`agents/cursor.cli-config.overlay.json`](../../.chezmoitemplates/agents/cursor.cli-config.overlay.json)
27	
28	```json
29	{
30	  "editor": { "vimMode": true }
31	}
32	```
33	
34	- `editor.vimMode = true` — universal preference; sibling `editor.fontSize` etc. survive the deep merge.
35	- **`permissions.allow` / `permissions.deny` arrays are intentionally NOT in the overlay.** `jq '. * $overlay'` replaces arrays wholesale at the same key path, so listing any entries here would clobber the user's live machine-specific allow-list on every `chezmoi apply`. Manage those per machine via the live file directly, or move to a `--argjson allow $merged` array-union approach if you ever need a shared baseline.
36	
37	### OpenCode — [`agents/opencode.overlay.json`](../../.chezmoitemplates/agents/opencode.overlay.json)
38	
39	```json
40	{
41	  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
42	  "autoupdate": true,
43	  "default_agent": "build",
44	  "small_model": "github-copilot/gpt-5-mini",
45	  "agent": { "title": { "reasoningEffort": "low" } },
46	  "provider": {
47	    "github-copilot": {
48	      "options": { "timeout": 600000 }
49	    }
50	  }
51	}
52	```
53	
54	- `$schema` — keeps editors aware of the schema for autocomplete.
55	- `autoupdate = true` — let the CLI self-update.
56	- `default_agent = "build"` — primary agent on TUI/CLI startup. Override per-session via `--agent` or the picker.
57	- `small_model = "github-copilot/gpt-5-mini"` — cheap model for title generation, summarisation, and other lightweight calls. Avoids billing Claude Opus quota for trivial tasks. Pairs with `agent.title.reasoningEffort = "low"`.
58	- `agent.title.reasoningEffort = "low"` — cheap completions for short title generation; sibling `agent.*` entries (per-agent provider, model overrides) survive.
59	- `provider.github-copilot.options.timeout = 600000` (10 min) — request-level timeout. Default is 5 min; bumped to give long Claude Opus generations more room before the SDK aborts the whole call. **Note**: `chunkTimeout` is intentionally NOT set here, see [docs/tools/opencode.md → Claude Opus stream stall](opencode.md#claude-opus-stream-stall-on-github-copilot) for the rationale (upstream bug [anomalyco/opencode#20466](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/20466) — SSE-chunk-timeout errors aren't retried, so setting `chunkTimeout` would convert silent hangs into hard failures with no recovery).
60	
61	### OpenCode TUI — [`agents/opencode.tui.overlay.json`](../../.chezmoitemplates/agents/opencode.tui.overlay.json)
62	
63	```json
64	{
65	  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/tui.json",
66	  "keybinds": { "leader": "ctrl+x" },
67	  "mouse": true,
68	  "diff_style": "auto",
69	  "scroll_acceleration": { "enabled": true }
70	}
71	```
72	
73	The TUI lives in a **separate file** from server/runtime config: `~/.config/opencode/tui.json` with its own schema `https://opencode.ai/tui.json`. See upstream docs:
74	
75	- [Config → TUI](https://opencode.ai/docs/config/#tui) — file location, schema URL, precedence
76	- [TUI → Configure → Options](https://opencode.ai/docs/tui/#options) — per-key semantics
77	
78	Key-by-key rationale:
79	
80	- `$schema = "https://opencode.ai/tui.json"` — TUI schema (different from `opencode.json`'s `config.json` schema). Lets editors validate + autocomplete.
81	- `keybinds.leader = "ctrl+x"` — explicit pin of the upstream default. Declaring it ensures muscle memory + the `<leader>` references in [docs/keybinds](https://opencode.ai/docs/keybinds/) survive any future upstream default change. The other ~80 keybind defaults are intentionally NOT pinned here — they stay tracking upstream so new actions added by OpenCode become available without overlay churn.
82	- `mouse = true` — explicit pin of the upstream default. Trades terminal-native select-to-copy for OpenCode's in-TUI mouse support (scroll, click).
83	- `diff_style = "auto"` — adapts diff layout to terminal width (vs `"stacked"` which forces single-column). Pinning the upstream default makes intent explicit.
84	- `scroll_acceleration.enabled = true` — macOS-style smooth/accelerated scrolling. Per upstream docs this **takes precedence over and overrides** `scroll_speed`, so we deliberately omit `scroll_speed` from the overlay (setting both would mislead — the latter would be silently ignored).
85	
86	What's intentionally NOT in the TUI overlay:
87	
88	- `theme` — left unset so OpenCode's auto light/dark detection stays in effect (matches the system theme just like `ghostty` and the `tmux` theme switcher in this repo).
89	- Individual `keybinds.*` entries beyond `leader` — see above. fzf's shell-level `Ctrl+T` and OpenCode's `variant_cycle = ctrl+t` do not collide because they live in disjoint namespaces (shell prompt vs OpenCode TUI).
90	- `username_toggle` / `tips_toggle` / `display_thinking` — these are persisted by the TUI's `/help` customisation panel at runtime. Pinning them in the overlay would clobber the user's last in-app choice on every `chezmoi apply`, same anti-pattern as managing `plugin` paths or auth tokens.
91	- `scroll_speed` — see `scroll_acceleration.enabled` above; OpenCode ignores `scroll_speed` whenever acceleration is enabled.
92	
93	### Codex — [`agents/codex.config.overlay.toml`](../../.chezmoitemplates/agents/codex.config.overlay.toml)
94	
95	```toml
96	personality = "pragmatic"
97	model = "gpt-5.4"
98	model_reasoning_effort = "xhigh"
99	
100	[features]
101	codex_hooks = true
102	unified_exec = true
103	shell_snapshot = true
104	steer = true
105	multi_agent = true
106	
107	[plugins."github@openai-curated"]
108	enabled = true
109	
110	[plugins."google-drive@openai-curated"]
111	enabled = true
112	
113	[plugins."computer-use@openai-bundled"]
114	enabled = true
115	```
116	
117	- Top-level model + reasoning preferences.
118	- `[features]` — opt into the experimental flags this user always wants on.
119	- `[plugins."<id>".enabled]` — curated plugin set; user-installed plugins appear under their own `[plugins."..."]` blocks and are preserved by the deep merge.
120	
121	## What is intentionally NOT managed
122	
123	| File / subtree | CLI | Why |
124	|---|---|---|
125	| `~/.cursor/{authInfo,auth*,privacyCache,statsigBootstrap,version,hasChangedDefaultModel,...}` | Cursor | Auth + telemetry; runtime-only. |
126	| `~/.cursor/{extensions,plugins,projects,worktrees,workers,browser-logs,chats,plans,prompt_history.json,argv.json,ide_state.json,agent-cli-state.json,ai-tracking,mcp.json,skills-cursor}` | Cursor | CLI-managed state, per-project, machine-local. |
127	| `~/.config/opencode/{node_modules,package.json,bun.lock,package-lock.json,plugins/}` | OpenCode | Node runtime + locally-installed plugin source trees. |
128	| `~/.config/opencode/tui.json` keys outside the TUI overlay (`theme`, `keybinds.*` other than `leader`, `username_toggle`, `tips_toggle`, `display_thinking`, `scroll_speed`) | OpenCode | TUI runtime customisation panel persists user choices here; overlay only pins stable preferences. |
129	| `~/.codex/auth.json` | Codex | OpenAI auth token. **Never** check in. |
130	| `~/.codex/[projects."<absolute-path>"]` | Codex | Per-project trust grants — absolute paths are machine-specific. **Round-tripped** by the modify_ script (see below). |
131	| `~/.codex/[marketplaces.<id>]` | Codex | Marketplace registrations with absolute `source = "/Users/.../.codex/.tmp/..."` paths. **Round-tripped**. |
132	| `~/.codex/{installation_id,history.jsonl,session_index.jsonl,sessions/,logs_*.sqlite*,state_*.sqlite,cache/,tmp/,log/,sqlite/,memories/,vendor_imports/,shell_snapshots/,models_cache.json,plugins/,skills/,rules/,ambient-suggestions/,version.json,AGENTS.md,.tmp/}` | Codex | Sessions, logs, sqlite, plugin/skills directories, machine-local notes. |
133	
134	The `.chezmoiignore.tmpl` presence-gates the entire `~/.cursor/`, `~/.codex/`, and `~/.config/opencode/` trees with a `stat` check so uninstalled CLIs never produce phantom directories.
135	
136	## How the Codex TOML merge works
137	
138	`jq` doesn't speak TOML and `mikefarah/yq`'s TOML emitter produces invalid output for keys with special characters (e.g. `github@openai-curated`). The Codex `modify_` script uses Python instead:
139	
140	1. Read live file into a `dict` via `tomllib` (Python 3.11+ built-in; `tomli` fallback for 3.10).
141	2. Pop `[projects]` and `[marketplaces]` subtrees into `state`.
142	3. Read overlay TOML into a `dict`.
143	4. Deep-merge: `live_minus_state <- overlay <- state`. Argument order is merge precedence (later wins). State wins last so per-project trust never gets clobbered by an overlay churn.
144	5. Emit TOML via a 30-line writer that quotes all non-bareword keys (handles `github@openai-curated` and `/Users/me/foo`-style project keys).
145	
146	The script falls through to passing the live file untouched if `python3` or `tomllib`/`tomli` are missing; chezmoi will skip the file for that apply.
147	
148	## OpenCode legacy `config.json` migration
149	
150	OpenCode docs now recommend `opencode.json` as the canonical filename, but installations from before that change use `config.json`. The repo manages only the modern filename; a one-shot script handles the migration:
151	
152	- [`run_once_before_50_opencode_migrate.sh.tmpl`](../../run_once_before_50_opencode_migrate.sh.tmpl) runs once per source-state hash, before chezmoi deploys files. It:
153	  1. No-ops if `~/.config/opencode/config.json` is absent.
154	  2. If only the legacy file exists: rename it to `opencode.json`.
155	  3. If both exist: deep-merge legacy into modern (modern wins on conflict, since it's presumed newer), then delete legacy.
156	
157	After this script runs, the `modify_opencode.json` overlay enforces the managed keys on the unified file. The legacy filename never reappears because OpenCode itself only writes `opencode.json` going forward.
158	
159	The migration script can be removed from the repo a few months after rollout (once all machines have run `chezmoi apply` at least once); it is idempotent and a no-op on fresh machines, so it's safe to leave indefinitely.
160	
161	## Refresh recipe
162	
163	To change what an overlay enforces, edit the corresponding `.chezmoitemplates/agents/<cli>.overlay.{json,toml}` file. Do **not** `chezmoi add` the live config — that would strip the `modify_` prefix and overwrite the script with the runtime file (which contains your secrets).
164	
165	To pull a new key from the live file into the overlay (e.g. you changed a Cursor permission you want shared):
166	
167	```bash
168	# 1. Inspect the live file
169	jq . ~/.cursor/cli-config.json
170	
171	# 2. Edit the overlay JSON / TOML and add the key
172	$EDITOR .chezmoitemplates/agents/cursor.cli-config.overlay.json
173	
174	# 3. Verify the rendered modify_ script outputs what you expect
175	chezmoi execute-template < dot_cursor/modify_cli-config.json.tmpl > /tmp/m.sh
176	chmod +x /tmp/m.sh
177	cat ~/.cursor/cli-config.json | /tmp/m.sh
178	
179	# 4. Apply
180	chezmoi apply
181	```
182	
183	## Tests
184	
185	[`tests/unit/agent_overlays.bats`](../../tests/unit/agent_overlays.bats) covers:
186	
187	- Each overlay enforces its declared keys.
188	- Live runtime keys outside the overlay are preserved verbatim.
189	- Codex `[projects.*]` and `[marketplaces.*]` round-trip unchanged (the round-trip property is the load-bearing invariant — break it and machines start clobbering each other's per-project trust).
190	- The modify_ scripts are idempotent (running output through the script again produces the same output).
191	- The OpenCode migration handles all three input states: legacy-only, both-present, neither-present.
192	- The Claude hook-aware merger (see next section): notify.sh added when missing; CodeIsland entries preserved; idempotency on re-apply; non-hook deep-merge preserves user siblings.
193	
194	Run with `just bats` (or directly: `bats tests/unit/agent_overlays.bats`).
195	
196	## CodeIsland integration (macOS-only)
197	
198	[CodeIsland](https://github.com/wxtsky/CodeIsland) is a macOS notch-area HUD (positioning analogous to [CodexBar](https://github.com/steipete/CodexBar)) that surfaces real-time activity from 11+ coding-agent CLIs (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini, Cursor, Copilot, OpenCode, AntiGravity, Trae, Qoder, Factory, CodeBuddy, Kimi). It works by injecting per-CLI hook entries that fire `~/.codeisland/codeisland-bridge` (or `codeisland-hook.sh`), which streams events over a Unix socket at `/tmp/codeisland-<uid>.sock` to the SwiftUI app.
199	
200	### Why macOS-only
201	
202	- Swift app, requires macOS 14 (Sonoma) or later.
203	- The notch UI assumes a MacBook display geometry.
204	- Distribution is via brew cask (`wxtsky/tap`) or `.dmg`.
205	
206	There is no Linux fallback — the wire format depends on the macOS-specific bridge binary and socket path. We deliberately install nothing for CodeIsland on Linux and skip all related concerns there.
207	
208	### Install
209	
210	The `codeisland` cask is added in [`dot_config/homebrew/Brewfile.darwin.tmpl`](../../dot_config/homebrew/Brewfile.darwin.tmpl) inside the `{{ if .installAiDesktopApps }}` block alongside the other agent desktop apps:
211	
212	```ruby
213	tap "wxtsky/tap"
214	cask "codeisland"
215	```
216	
217	### How we coexist with the app
218	
219	CodeIsland's settings panel calls itself "Auto hook install" with "auto-repair and version tracking" — meaning the **app actively writes and re-writes** hook entries into each detected CLI's config on every launch. Two coexistence patterns:
220	
221	> **Note (2026-04-25)**: CodeIsland v1.0.23 dropped `ExitPlanMode` from the default `HookServer.autoApproveTools` whitelist — plan-mode exit now prompts a real confirm dialog, and Settings → Behavior → "Auto-approve Tools" lets users toggle individual tools. See [`pitfalls/codeisland-auto-approves-permissionrequest.md`](../../pitfalls/codeisland-auto-approves-permissionrequest.md). Our merger continues to *additively* preserve every CodeIsland hook entry — no subtractive logic was added, because the upstream fix is the right path and the `PermissionRequest` hook is now a legitimate input source for the notch popup, not a bypass mechanism.
222	
223	#### Pattern A — Sidecar files (always-ignored)
224	
225	CLIs whose hooks live in a dedicated sidecar (containing nothing but CodeIsland hooks) are simply unmanaged by chezmoi. Concretely:
226	
227	| File | CLI | Why unmanaged |
228	|------|-----|---------------|
229	| `~/.codex/hooks.json` | Codex | Pure CodeIsland sidecar (also extended by Superset's notify.sh in some setups, but that's installed by Superset, not us) |
230	| `~/.cursor/hooks.json` | Cursor | Same |
231	| `~/.copilot/hooks/codeisland.json` | GitHub Copilot CLI | Pure CodeIsland sidecar |
232	| `~/.gemini/settings.json` | Gemini CLI | Currently nothing else to enforce there |
233	| `~/.antigravity/settings.json` | AntiGravity (CLI, not the editor) | Currently nothing else to enforce there |
234	
235	These paths are added to [`.chezmoiignore.tmpl`](../../.chezmoiignore.tmpl) as **always-ignore** so accidentally running `chezmoi add ~/.codex/hooks.json` won't pull a CodeIsland-owned file into the source tree (which would clobber the app's runtime updates and create a ping-pong with its auto-installer).
236	
237	If you later want to manage non-hook prefs in `~/.gemini/settings.json` or `~/.antigravity/settings.json`, write a `modify_` overlay that follows the hook-aware pattern below — and remove the corresponding ignore line.
238	
239	#### Pattern B — Mixed files (hook-aware merger)
240	
241	Files where stable user prefs and CodeIsland hooks coexist need a smarter overlay. Currently the only such file is **`~/.claude/settings.json`** — Claude Code stores model selection, plugins, statusLine, and `permissions.defaultMode` in the same file as `hooks.<event>` arrays. A naive `jq '. * $overlay'` deep-merge replaces arrays wholesale: declaring a `hooks.Notification` entry in our overlay would silently delete every CodeIsland entry on each `chezmoi apply`, then CodeIsland would re-install on next launch — endless ping-pong producing diff noise and broken integrations.
242	
243	[`dot_claude/modify_settings.json`](../../dot_claude/modify_settings.json) solves this with a hook-aware merger:
244	
245	1. **Non-hook keys** (`enabledPlugins`, `extraKnownMarketplaces`, `skipDangerousModePermissionPrompt`, `permissions.defaultMode`, `statusLine`, …) deep-merge normally via `base * overlay_no_hooks`. Note: `permissions.defaultMode = "bypassPermissions"` is set deliberately to work around Claude Code resetting the active permission mode after every interactive prompt (`AskUserQuestion`, CodeIsland popup, remote-control inject); see [`pitfalls/claude-code-permission-mode-resets-after-interactive-prompt.md`](../../pitfalls/claude-code-permission-mode-resets-after-interactive-prompt.md). The deep-merge writes the `defaultMode` scalar without touching sibling `permissions.allow` / `permissions.deny` arrays — those remain machine-local.
246	2. **`hooks.<event>` arrays** are merged additively: for each event the overlay declares, append entries whose `.hooks[0].command` isn't already represented in the live array (string-equality match). Live entries are preserved verbatim, no entry is ever removed.
247	
248	The full filter (jq):
249	
250	```jq
251	. as $base
252	| ($overlay | del(.hooks)) as $non_hook_overlay
253	| ($overlay.hooks // {}) as $overlay_hooks
254	| ($base * $non_hook_overlay) as $merged
255	| $merged
256	| .hooks = (
257	    ($merged.hooks // {}) as $live_hooks
258	    | reduce ($overlay_hooks | to_entries[]) as $ev (
259	        $live_hooks;
260	        .[$ev.key] = (
261	          (.[$ev.key] // []) as $live_arr
262	          | ($live_arr | map(.hooks[0].command? // "")) as $live_cmds
263	          | $live_arr + (
264	              $ev.value
265	              | map(select(
266	                  (.hooks[0].command? // "") as $cmd
267	                  | ($cmd == "") or (($live_cmds | index($cmd)) == null)
268	                ))
269	            )
270	        )
271	      )
272	  )
273	```
274	
275	Test coverage in `tests/unit/agent_overlays.bats`:
276	
277	- `claude modify_settings: notify.sh added to empty hooks, codeisland entries preserved` — proves the additive append works without removing CodeIsland entries.
278	- `claude modify_settings: idempotent when notify.sh already present` — proves no duplicate appears on re-apply.
279	- `claude modify_settings: empty live file produces overlay-only output` — bootstrap on a fresh machine.
280	- `claude modify_settings: non-hook deep-merge preserves siblings` — proves user-added plugins/marketplaces survive.
281	
282	> **Sibling overlay**: `~/.claude/keybindings.json` is managed by a separate, simpler `modify_` script — [`dot_claude/modify_keybindings.json`](../../dot_claude/modify_keybindings.json). It is NOT hook-aware (CodeIsland doesn't write to keybindings.json). See [Claude Code keybindings](claude-code-keybindings.md) for its design, the `chat:cycleMode`-only mode-jump limitation, and how to add personal binding overrides.
283	
284	### Future work (deferred)
285	
286	- **Apprise-to-webhook expansion of `~/.claude/hooks/notify.sh`**: the script already calls `apprise --tag desktop` for local OS notifications. Could be extended to also fire `apprise --tag webhook` for remote chat-app delivery (Slack, Discord, Telegram, …) using URLs configured in `~/.config/apprise/apprise.yaml`. Open question: noise filtering — should webhook fire on every `Notification`/`Stop`, or only on permission-request and session-end? Likely needs an env-var gate (`CLAUDE_NOTIFY_WEBHOOK=1`) so each machine opts in. Track in a separate change.
287	- **Managed overlays for `~/.gemini/settings.json` and `~/.antigravity/settings.json`**: defer until concrete prefs need enforcing. When added, follow the hook-aware merger pattern from Claude (each of those files also has CodeIsland-injected `hooks` blocks today).
288
```

10	"""
11	fleet_apply.py — Run `chezmoi update --init` (or `apply` / `diff`) across a
12	fleet of remote hosts in parallel, with optional sudo password injection.
13	
14	Why this exists:
15	    Pushing dotfile changes to N machines by hand (ssh, type password, wait,
16	    grep logs) is error-prone. This wraps that flow:
17	
18	      * Host list + connection details live in ~/.config/fleet/machines.toml
19	      * Connection prefers ssh_config alias (ProxyJump, IdentityAgent, etc. all
20	        kept) — falls back to explicit hostname/user/port/identity_file.
21	      * Sudo password sources: plaintext (TOML), interactive prompt (asked once
22	        at startup), Bitwarden CLI (`bw get password <item>`), or omitted.
23	      * Per-host `no_root_machine = true` skips sudo entirely (matches the
24	        chezmoi `noRoot=true` init choice on that host).
25	      * Live Rich table of progress + per-host log files under
26	        logs/fleet-apply/<UTC-timestamp>/<host>.log
27	
28	Exit code: number of failed hosts (0 = all good, capped at 125).
29	
30	See docs/this_repo/fleet-apply.md for full schema, examples, troubleshooting.
31	"""
32	from __future__ import annotations
33	
34	import asyncio
35	import dataclasses
36	import getpass
37	import os
38	import re
39	import shlex
40	import subprocess
41	import sys
42	import time
43	import tomllib
44	from datetime import datetime, timezone
45	from pathlib import Path
46	from typing import Annotated, Literal
47	
48	import asyncssh
49	import tyro
50	from rich.console import Console
51	from rich.live import Live
52	from rich.table import Table
53	
54	
55	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
56	# Data model
57	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
58	
59	PasswordSourceType = Literal["plain", "prompt", "bitwarden", "none"]
60	
61	
62	@dataclasses.dataclass
63	class Host:
64	    """One remote machine. See machines.toml schema in docs."""
65	
66	    name: str
67	    ssh_alias: str | None = None
68	    hostname: str | None = None
69	    user: str | None = None
70	    port: int | None = None
71	    identity_file: str | None = None
72	    no_root_machine: bool = False
73	    chezmoi_path: str = "auto"
74	    # When True, bypass SSH entirely and run chezmoi as a local
75	    # subprocess on the orchestrator machine. Useful for including the
76	    # control box itself in a fleet apply (e.g. you keep your own
77	    # workstation in sync with the same `just fleet-apply` invocation).
78	    # Local hosts skip all SSH-specific config (ssh_alias/hostname/
79	    # user/port/identity_file are ignored) and reuse the caller's
80	    # ambient PATH so chezmoi_path = "auto" still works without the
81	    # remote-style PATH augmentation. Sudo password injection is
82	    # skipped — chezmoi inherits the caller's tty/sudoers state.
83	    local: bool = False
84	    extra_env: dict[str, str] = dataclasses.field(default_factory=dict)
85	    # Resolved later (not from TOML directly)
86	    password_source_type: PasswordSourceType = "none"
87	    password_source_arg: str | None = None  # plain value, bw item id, etc.
88	    sudo_password: str | None = None  # populated by resolve_passwords()
89	
90	
91	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
92	# TOML loading
93	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
94	
95	DEFAULT_CONFIG_PATH = Path(
96	    os.environ.get("FLEET_CONFIG")
97	    or (Path.home() / ".config" / "fleet" / "machines.toml")
98	).expanduser()
99

101	def load_hosts(path: Path) -> tuple[list[Host], dict]:
102	    """Parse machines.toml -> ([Host, ...], defaults dict).
103	
104	    Merges [defaults] into each host (host overrides defaults). The
105	    `password_source` table is normalized into (type, arg) on Host.
106	    """
107	    if not path.exists():
108	        raise FileNotFoundError(
109	            f"Fleet config not found: {path}\n"
110	            f"Hint: chezmoi apply seeds ~/.config/fleet/machines.toml — edit it "
111	            f"to list your machines, or pass --config PATH."
112	        )
113	    with path.open("rb") as f:
114	        data = tomllib.load(f)
115	
116	    defaults = data.get("defaults", {}) or {}
117	    raw_hosts = data.get("hosts", []) or []
118	    if not raw_hosts:
119	        raise ValueError(f"{path}: no [[hosts]] entries defined.")
120	
121	    hosts: list[Host] = []
122	    seen_names: set[str] = set()
123	    for idx, raw in enumerate(raw_hosts):
124	        name = raw.get("name")
125	        if not name:
126	            raise ValueError(f"{path}: [[hosts]][{idx}] missing required `name`.")
127	        if name in seen_names:
128	            raise ValueError(f"{path}: duplicate host name {name!r}.")
129	        seen_names.add(name)
130	
131	        merged = {**defaults, **raw}
132	        ps = merged.pop("password_source", None) or {}
133	        ps_type = (ps.get("type") or "none").lower()
134	        if ps_type not in ("plain", "prompt", "bitwarden", "none"):
135	            raise ValueError(
136	                f"{path}: host {name!r} has invalid password_source.type={ps_type!r}"
137	            )
138	        ps_arg = ps.get("value") if ps_type == "plain" else ps.get("item")
139	
140	        # Drop keys that aren't Host fields (e.g. defaults-only knobs we read elsewhere).
141	        host_fields = {f.name for f in dataclasses.fields(Host)}
142	        host_kwargs = {k: v for k, v in merged.items() if k in host_fields}
143	        host = Host(
144	            **host_kwargs,
145	            password_source_type=ps_type,  # type: ignore[arg-type]
146	            password_source_arg=ps_arg,
147	        )
148	
149	        # Validation: at least one of ssh_alias / hostname (skipped for local hosts).
150	        if not host.local and not host.ssh_alias and not host.hostname:

2	# ssh-to-bitwarden - Import SSH key pairs into Bitwarden vault
3	#
4	# Scans a directory (default: ~/.ssh) for SSH private keys, shows an
5	# interactive menu for selecting which keys to import, then creates
6	# Bitwarden vault items for each selected key.
7	#
8	# Requirements: bw (Bitwarden CLI >= 2024.x), jq, ssh-keygen
9	#
10	# Usage:
11	#   ssh-to-bitwarden [OPTIONS]
12	#
13	# Options:
14	#   -d, --dir DIR       Directory to scan (default: ~/.ssh)
15	#   -a, --all           Import all discovered keys without prompting
16	#   -n, --dry-run       Show what would be imported without creating items
17	#   -p, --prefix STR    Prefix for Bitwarden item names (default: "SSH")
18	#   -h, --help          Show this help message
19	
20	set -euo pipefail
21	
22	# ── Defaults ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
23	SSH_DIR="$HOME/.ssh"
24	IMPORT_ALL=false
25	DRY_RUN=false
26	NAME_PREFIX="SSH"
27	
28	# Field separator for internal record passing (ASCII Unit Separator)
29	FS=$'\x1f'
30	
31	# ── Colors (disabled if not a terminal) ───────────────────────────────
32	if [ -t 1 ]; then
33	  BOLD='\033[1m'    DIM='\033[2m'    RESET='\033[0m'
34	  GREEN='\033[32m'  YELLOW='\033[33m' RED='\033[31m' CYAN='\033[36m'
35	else
36	  BOLD='' DIM='' RESET='' GREEN='' YELLOW='' RED='' CYAN=''
37	fi
38	
39	# ── Helpers ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
40	info()  { printf "${CYAN}[INFO]${RESET}  %s\n" "$*"; }
41	ok()    { printf "${GREEN}[OK]${RESET}    %s\n" "$*"; }
42	warn()  { printf "${YELLOW}[WARN]${RESET}  %s\n" "$*"; }
43	error() { printf "${RED}[ERROR]${RESET} %s\n" "$*" >&2; }
44	skip()  { printf "${DIM}[SKIP]${RESET}  %s\n" "$*"; }
45	
46	usage() {
47	  cat <<'USAGE'
48	ssh-to-bitwarden - Import SSH key pairs into Bitwarden vault
49	
50	Usage:
51	  ssh-to-bitwarden [OPTIONS]
52	
53	Options:
54	  -d, --dir DIR       Directory to scan (default: ~/.ssh)
55	  -a, --all           Import all discovered keys without prompting
56	  -n, --dry-run       Show what would be imported without creating items
57	  -p, --prefix STR    Prefix for Bitwarden item names (default: "SSH")
58	  -h, --help          Show this help message
59	
60	Examples:
61	  ssh-to-bitwarden                  # Interactive mode, scan ~/.ssh
62	  ssh-to-bitwarden --all            # Import all keys without prompting
63	  ssh-to-bitwarden -d /tmp/keys     # Scan a custom directory
64	  ssh-to-bitwarden --dry-run        # Preview what would be imported
65	USAGE
66	  exit 0
67	}
68	
69	# ── Parse arguments ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
70	while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
71	  case "$1" in
72	    -d|--dir)     SSH_DIR="$2"; shift 2 ;;
73	    -a|--all)     IMPORT_ALL=true; shift ;;
74	    -n|--dry-run) DRY_RUN=true; shift ;;
75	    -p|--prefix)  NAME_PREFIX="$2"; shift 2 ;;
76	    -h|--help)    usage ;;
77	    *)            error "Unknown option: $1"; usage ;;
78	  esac
79	done
80	
81	# ── Dependency checks ────────────────────────────────────────────────
82	for cmd in bw jq ssh-keygen; do
83	  if ! command -v "$cmd" &>/dev/null; then
84	    error "Required command '$cmd' not found. Please install it first."
85	    exit 1
86	  fi
87	done
88	
89	# ── Discover SSH private keys ────────────────────────────────────────
90	# Scans the given directory for files that look like SSH private keys.
91	# Outputs one file path per line.
92	discover_keys() {
93	  local dir="$1"
94	
95	  if [ ! -d "$dir" ]; then
96	    error "Directory not found: $dir"
97	    exit 1
98	  fi
99	
100	  while IFS= read -r -d '' file; do
101	    local name
102	    name=$(basename "$file")
103	
104	    # Skip known non-key files
105	    case "$name" in
106	      *.pub|known_hosts*|config|authorized_keys*|*.swp|*.swo|*~|*.un~|*.log) continue ;;
107	    esac
108	
109	    # Check if file begins with a PEM private key header
110	    if head -1 "$file" 2>/dev/null | grep -q '^\-\-\-\-\-BEGIN.*PRIV***KEY\-\-\-\-\-'; then
111	      echo "$file"
112	    fi
113	  done < <(find "$dir" -maxdepth 1 -type f -print0 2>/dev/null)
114	}
115	
116	# ── Extract key metadata ─────────────────────────────────────────────
117	# Returns a FS-delimited record:
118	#   privkey FS pubkey FS fingerprint FS key_type FS basename
119	get_key_info() {
120	  local privkey="$1"
121	  local pubkey="${privkey}.pub"
122	  local name
123	  name=$(basename "$privkey")
124	
125	  local fingerprint="N/A"
126	  local key_type="unknown"
127	
128	  # Look for a matching .pub file
129	  if [ ! -f "$pubkey" ]; then
130	    local stem="${privkey%.*}"
131	    if [ -f "${stem}.pub" ]; then
132	      pubkey="${stem}.pub"
133	    else
134	      pubkey=""
135	    fi
136	  fi
137	
138	  # Extract fingerprint and type from ssh-keygen
139	  # Output format: "bits SHA256:xxx comment (TYPE)"
140	  local keygen_src="${pubkey:-$privkey}"
141	  local keygen_output
142	  keygen_output=$(ssh-keygen -lf "$keygen_src" 2>/dev/null) || true
143	
144	  if [ -n "$keygen_output" ]; then
145	    fingerprint=$(awk '{print $2}' <<< "$keygen_output")
146	    key_type=$(grep -oE '\([A-Za-z0-9_-]+\)\s*$' <<< "$keygen_output" | tr -d '() ') || key_type="unknown"
147	    [ -z "$key_type" ] && key_type="unknown"
148	  fi
149	
150	  printf '%s' "${privkey}${FS}${pubkey}${FS}${fingerprint}${FS}${key_type}${FS}${name}"
```

```text
1	# fzf Quick Reference
2	
3	[fzf](https://github.com/junegunn/fzf) — command-line fuzzy finder.
4	
5	Config source: `dot_config/zsh/tools/10_fzf.zsh`
6	
7	---
8	
9	## Shell Keybindings
10	
11	| Key | Action | Preview |
12	|-----|--------|---------|
13	| `Ctrl+T` | Insert fuzzy-matched file path at cursor | `bat` syntax highlight (500 lines) |
14	| `Ctrl+R` | Fuzzy search command history | — |
15	| `Alt+C` | Fuzzy-match directory and `cd` into it | `eza --tree` (200 lines) |
16	
17	---
18	
19	## Environment Variables
20	
21	```bash
22	# Base options applied to all fzf invocations
23	FZF_DEFAULT_OPTS="--height 40% --layout=reverse --border"
24	
25	# Use fd instead of find (respects .gitignore, faster)
26	FZF_DEFAULT_COMMAND="fd --hidden --strip-cwd-prefix --exclude .git"
27	
28	# Ctrl+T: file picker
29	FZF_CTRL_T_COMMAND="fd --hidden --strip-cwd-prefix --exclude .git"
30	FZF_CTRL_T_OPTS="--preview 'bat -n --color=always --line-range :500 {}'"
31	
32	# Alt+C: directory picker
33	FZF_ALT_C_COMMAND="fd --type=d --hidden --strip-cwd-prefix --exclude .git"
34	FZF_ALT_C_OPTS="--preview 'eza --tree --color=always {} | head -200'"
35	```
36	
37	---
38	
39	## Tab Completion Preview (`_fzf_comprun`)
40	
41	When using fzf-powered tab completion, preview varies by command:
42	
43	| Command | Preview |
44	|---------|---------|
45	| `cd` | `eza --tree --color=always` (fallback: `tree -C`) |
46	| `export`, `unset` | `echo ${<var>}` — shows current variable value |
47	| `ssh` | `dig <host>` — DNS lookup |
48	| *(default)* | `bat -n --color=always --line-range :500` |
49	
50	---
51	
52	## fzf-tmux Integration
53	
54	The `sesh-sessions` widget (bound to `Alt+S`) uses `fzf-tmux -p 80%,70%` to open a
55	floating popup inside tmux. See `docs/tools/sesh.md` for session picker keybindings.
56	
57	---
58	
59	## Tips
60	
61	- **Fuzzy syntax**: space-separated tokens are AND'd; `!` negates; `^` anchors start; `$` anchors end
62	  - Example: `^foo bar !baz$` — starts with "foo", contains "bar", does not end with "baz"
63	- **Multi-select**: pass `--multi` (or `-m`) to enable `Tab`/`Shift+Tab` for multi-selection
64	- **Preview toggle**: `Ctrl+/` toggles the preview pane (built-in default)
65
```
</details></tool-use>

 `./docs/tools/web-reader.md`

```text
1	# Read the Web as Markdown in the Terminal
2	
3	Focus-mode reading (think Safari Reader / Firefox Reader View) but driven from a terminal: fetch a page, strip it down to the article body, render as markdown in a pager. Useful for offline reading, piping into LLMs, or just avoiding browser chrome when you already live in the shell.
4	
5	This repo ships four interchangeable readers covering the common combinations of **remote vs local**, **article extraction vs full page**, and **different extractor strategies**. Pick the one that fits the page at hand.
6	
7	## TL;DR
8	
9	| Command | Extractor | Local / remote | Best for |
10	|---------|-----------|----------------|----------|
11	| `readurl <url>` | [Jina AI Reader](https://jina.ai/reader) (`r.jina.ai`) | remote | Default. Any page, zero local deps beyond `glow`. Fast. |
12	| `readlocal <url>` | [trafilatura](https://trafilatura.readthedocs.io/) | local (Python) | Privacy-sensitive or offline. Well-tuned for news/blog articles. |
13	| `readnode <url>` | [readability-cli](https://gitlab.com/gardenappl/readability-cli) (Mozilla Readability port) | local (Node) | Same algorithm as Firefox/Safari Reader View. Often the best article fidelity. |
14	| `readraw <url>` | `curl \| pandoc -f html -t gfm` | local | Escape hatch: docs / reference pages where article extraction strips too much. |
15	
16	All four pipe into [`glow`](https://github.com/charmbracelet/glow) for rendering and paging, and all four wrap the fetch in `try_direct_then_proxy` so pages reachable without a proxy pay zero overhead.
17	
18	Source: `dot_config/zsh/tools/55_web_reader.zsh` (readers) and `dot_config/zsh/tools/50_networking.zsh` (proxy helpers).
19	
20	## The landscape — why four tools, not one
21	
22	"Read a webpage as markdown" decomposes into three independent choices:
23	
24	1. **Fetch** — `curl`, headless browser (for JS-heavy pages), or a remote service that fetches on your behalf.
25	2. **Extract** — strip navigation, ads, comments, footers; keep the article. Or don't, if you want the whole page.
26	3. **Render** — markdown into the terminal; `glow`, `mdcat`, or plain stdout.
27	
28	No single tool owns the full pipeline well:
29	
30	- [**Jina AI Reader**](https://jina.ai/reader) collapses fetch + extract into a single HTTP GET: `https://r.jina.ai/<url>` returns ready-to-read markdown. Zero install. Trade-offs: remote service (privacy / availability), and may itself be blocked from some networks — fall back through a proxy in that case.
31	- [**trafilatura**](https://trafilatura.readthedocs.io/) is a Python library + CLI focused on article extraction. Local, offline, battle-tested on news/blog corpora. Weakness: built-in fetcher is bare — sites with heavy anti-bot measures can trip it.
32	- [**readability-cli**](https://gitlab.com/gardenappl/readability-cli) (binary: `readable`) wraps Mozilla's Readability library — the exact algorithm behind Firefox / Safari Reader View. Excellent fidelity on article-shaped pages.
33	- [**pandoc**](https://pandoc.org/) does no extraction; it converts full HTML to GFM markdown. Handy when the "article body" is the whole page (e.g. a man-page-style spec, a GitHub README rendered HTML, a single-column docs page).
34	
35	Other options considered but not wired up (install manually if you want them):
36	
37	- [**monolith**](https://github.com/Y2Z/monolith) — saves a whole page (+ assets) as a single-file HTML. Good for archival, but doesn't help with focus reading.
38	- [**w3m / lynx / elinks -dump**](https://w3m.sourceforge.net/) — text-mode browsers that render to plaintext (not markdown). Useful when all else fails; no extraction.
39	- [**Postlight Parser**](https://github.com/postlight/parser) — older, less maintained than readability-cli, same family.
40	- [**single-file-cli**](https://github.com/gildas-lormeau/single-file-cli) — headless-Chrome based; overkill for reading, great for archival.
41	- [**mdcat**](https://github.com/swsnr/mdcat) — alternative markdown renderer (hyperlinked terminals); `glow -p` remains the default here because it pages.
42	
43	## Usage
44	
45	```bash
46	# jina.ai Reader — default, zero-install (beyond glow)
47	readurl nytimes.com/2024/.../some-article
48	
49	# trafilatura — fully local, no third-party
50	readlocal example.com/some-article
```
</details></tool-use>

```text
1	# aicapture — AI review of past shell commands
2	
3	Capture a past shell command's block from tmux scrollback, pipe it to a coding-agent CLI (Claude Code / OpenCode / Codex / Cursor Agent) in non-interactive mode, get back a fix or explanation. Advisory by default: agent prints suggestions, doesn't touch files.
4	
5	Built on [OSC 133 semantic prompts](https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/Per_Bothner/specifications/blob/master/proposals/semantic-prompts.md) — the shell emits `A`/`C`/`D` line-attribute markers, tmux stores them, our helpers navigate by them. For background on how this compares to `thefuck`, Warp, `wut`, `tmuxai`, `atuin`, etc., see [instant-llm-fix-prior-art.md](../this_repo/instant-llm-fix-prior-art.md).
6	
7	## Quick start
8	
9	```sh
10	# Any command that produced useful output or an error…
11	cargo build --release
12	
13	# …is one keystroke away from a diagnose + fix:
14	aifix
15	```
16	
17	Output in your terminal:
18	
19	```
20	aifix ← block -1
21	⠋ claude haiku (json)…                                  # spinner while agent thinks
22	claude (claude-haiku-4-5-20251001) | in=12 out=87 cache=(r:24402,w:12487) | cost=$0.0008 3812ms
23	
24	## Fix for `cargo build` error
25	
26	Your `Cargo.toml` is missing the `serde` dependency. Add:
27	
28	    [dependencies]
29	    serde = { version = "1.0", features = ["derive"] }
30	
31	Then re-run `cargo build --release`.
32	```
33	
34	Reply is rendered as Markdown via `glow` (auto-falls back to `bat --language=md`, then raw text if neither is installed).
35	
36	## Commands
37	
38	### Capture (no AI call)
39	
40	Each prints captured text to stdout (pipe-friendly) **and** copies it to the system clipboard via tmux's OSC 52 bridge (works over SSH). Defaults to N=1 (most recent); pass a positive integer for N-back lookback.
41	
42	| Command | Scope |
43	|---|---|
44	| `cpcmd [N]` | Nth-latest command's **input line** (from zsh history — works outside tmux too) |
45	| `cpout [N]` | Nth-latest command's **output** only (via tmux + OSC 133) |
46	| `cpblock [N]` | Nth-latest command's **full block**: prompt + input + output (Warp-style) |
47	
48	```sh
49	cpblock                          # last block → clipboard + stdout
50	cpblock 3                        # 3rd-latest
51	cpout 2 | tee /tmp/snapshot.log  # pipe output to file while also copying
52	cpcmd                            # just the command string (no output)
53	```
54	
55	### AI review
56	
57	Same positional `[N]` as the capture helpers, plus flags:
58	
59	| Command | Default prompt |
60	|---|---|
61	| `aifix [N]` | *"Diagnose any errors and suggest a concrete fix. Be brief and specific."* |
62	| `aiexplain [N]` | *"Explain what happened in plain language. Be concise."* |
63	
64	Both accept:
65	
66	- `-a AGENT` — `claude` / `opencode` / `codex` / `cursor-agent`. Default: auto-detect (first one found on `$PATH`).
67	- `-p PROMPT` — override the default prompt.
68	- `--raw` — skip glow/bat prettify; print the agent's raw Markdown text.
69	- `--no-meta` — suppress the stderr metadata line (model / tokens / cost / duration).
70	- `-h` / `--help` — print the full signature and current env-var values.
71	
72	```sh
73	aifix                               # last block, default fix prompt
74	aifix 3 -a opencode                 # 3rd-latest, force OpenCode
75	aifix -p "is this safe on prod?"    # custom prompt
76	aiexplain 2 --raw                   # no prettify
77	aifix --no-meta | tee /tmp/ans.md   # pipe-friendly
78	```
79	
80	### Interactive TUI
81	
82	```sh
83	aiblock
84	```
85	
86	Launches a [questionary](https://github.com/tmbo/questionary) + [rich](https://github.com/Textualize/rich) TUI ([`scripts/aiblock.py`](../../scripts/aiblock.py)) that walks through:
87	
88	1. **Checkbox picker** over the last 20 commands. Space toggles, Enter confirms. Picking none defaults to "last block".
89	2. **Preview** — each selected block shown in its own rich panel (multi-select concatenates in chronological order with `--- Block -N ---` separators so the agent can tell the turns apart).
90	3. **Prompt edit** — default is the `aifix` fix-prompt; edit inline.
91	4. **Action** — one of:
92	   - *Print reply here* — rendered as Markdown in a rich panel with the metadata as subtitle.
93	   - *Copy reply to clipboard* — via tmux OSC 52 / pbcopy / xclip / xsel / wl-copy.
94	   - *Spawn new tmux window running `<agent>`* — opens a fresh interactive agent session with your selected blocks pre-loaded into tmux's `aiblock` paste-buffer. Pull via `prefix + =`.
95	
96	The TUI depends on `uv` (PEP 723 inline deps) — no separate install step required; first run populates the uv cache.
97	
98	## Non-tmux alternatives
99	
100	When you're not in tmux (VSCode integrated terminal, bare Ghostty without tmux, quick SSH session), `cpblock` / `aifix` / `aiexplain` / `aiblock` can't see scrollback — they depend on tmux's OSC 133 line attributes. Three Tier 1 wrappers cover the common cases without magic (no shell hooks, no PTY proxy, no `script(1)` wrapping — see [`backlog/ai-capture-non-tmux-output.md`](../../backlog/ai-capture-non-tmux-output.md) for why we reject those paths):
101	
102	| Command | Source of context | Typical use |
103	|---|---|---|
104	| `aifix-stdin` | whatever you pipe in | `tail -100 build.log \| aifix-stdin` |
105	| `aifix-run -- CMD [ARG...]` | runs `CMD`, tees stdout+stderr to a log, reviews | `aifix-run -- cargo build --release` |
106	| `aifix-rerun` | re-executes the previous shell command (confirm prompt) | `aifix-rerun` after a transient error |
107	
108	All three accept the same flags as `aifix` (`-a AGENT` / `-p PROMPT` / `--raw` / `--no-meta`). `aifix-rerun` adds `-y` to skip the "⚠ side effects" confirmation. Default prompt for each is the `aifix` "diagnose + fix"; use `-p "explain what happened"` if you want the explain behaviour.
109	
110	```sh
111	# stdin — compose with any producer
112	tail -200 /var/log/nginx/error.log | aifix-stdin
113	curl -sS https://weird.api/thing | aifix-stdin -p "what is this JSON telling me?"
114	aifix-stdin < /tmp/build-fail.log
115	
116	# run — capture a fresh invocation (double-run safe, no prior history needed)
117	aifix-run -- ls /missing
118	aifix-run -p "is this safe on prod?" -- ansible-playbook deploy.yml
119	
120	# rerun — thefuck-style, re-execute last cmd. Confirms by default.
121	mvn compile      # fails
122	aifix-rerun      # "⚠ side effects…  Proceed? [y/N]"
123	aifix-rerun -y   # skip confirm
124	```
125	
126	**isatty caveat** for `aifix-run`: teeing makes CMD's stdout a pipe, so TUI apps (vim, less, htop) render in degraded mode. Don't `aifix-run` an interactive tool — pipe its log file via `aifix-stdin` after the fact instead.
127	
128	**Side-effect warning** for `aifix-rerun`: re-running `rm`, `curl -X POST`, `git push`, migrations, etc. is dangerous. The confirmation prompt is there for a reason; don't `-y` without reading what will be re-executed.
129	
130	## Configuration
131	
132	Put any of these in `~/.zshrc`, a `99_local_*.zsh` override, or export them per-session:
133	
134	```sh
135	# Model per agent (auto-detected order: claude → opencode → codex → cursor-agent)
136	export AICAP_CLAUDE_MODEL=haiku                              # alias or full name (e.g. claude-sonnet-4-6)
137	export AICAP_OPENCODE_MODEL=github-copilot/claude-haiku-4.5  # provider/model format
138	export AICAP_CODEX_MODEL=gpt-5-mini
139	export AICAP_CURSOR_MODEL=                                    # empty = cursor-agent picks
140	
141	# Output behaviour
142	export AICAP_SHOW_METADATA=1   # 0 to mute the stderr "claude (...) | in=... cost=..." line
143	export AICAP_PRETTIFY=1        # 0 to always print raw Markdown (skip glow/bat)
144	export AICAP_SPINNER=1         # 0 to disable the stderr spinner animation
145	```
146	
147	Check current settings any time with `aifix --help`.
148	
149	Defaults are tuned for Haiku-class models — fast (~5s round-trip) and cheap (~$0.001/call with cache hits). If you want Opus/Sonnet for harder diagnoses, set `AICAP_CLAUDE_MODEL=sonnet` either globally or per-invocation:
150
```

**File:** `executable_menu-theme.sh` (line 4)

NAME_PREFIX="SSH"

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# Top-level tmux popup menu — invoked by `prefix + Space`.
3	#
4	# Why a script (not inline `display-menu` in keybindings.conf):
5	#   1. tmux's command parser stops at literal `;`, `{`, `}` even inside
6	#      nested quotes. With ~50 menu rows full of fzf binds and shell
7	#      one-liners, escaping became fragile and broke silently.
8	#   2. tmux `display-menu` does not paginate. If the menu is taller than
9	#      the terminal, the entire popup is suppressed with no error. By
10	#      generating the menu here we can read $TMUX client_height and
11	#      auto-trim low-frequency rows when small.
12	#   3. Submenus are normal `tmux display-menu` invocations from rows;
13	#      they don't share quoting context with the parent menu.
14	#
15	# Submenus live in sibling scripts:
16	#   menu-layouts.sh, menu-session.sh, menu-sesh.sh,
17	#   menu-popups.sh, menu-theme.sh, menu-system.sh, menu-agents.sh
18	#
19	# See: pitfalls/tmux-display-menu-silent-parse-failure.md
20	
21	set -euo pipefail
22	
23	H=$(tmux display-message -p '#{client_height}')
24	DIR=~/.config/tmux
25	
26	# Tier 0: ALWAYS shown (highest frequency, ~7 rows + 2 separators)
27	declare -a tier0=(
28	  "Last window"  Tab "last-window"
29	  "Last pane"    P   "last-pane"
30	  ""             ""  ""
31	  "Choose win"   w   "choose-tree -Zw"
32	  "Choose sess"  s   "choose-tree -Zs"
33	  "Pane #s"      q   "display-panes -d 0"
34	  ""             ""  ""
35	  "Sesh picker"  g   "run-shell '$DIR/sesh-picker.sh'"
36	  "Lazygit"      G   "display-popup -E -w 90% -h 90% -d '#{pane_current_path}' -T ' lazygit ' 'lazygit'"
37	)
38	
39	# Tier 1: shown when height >= 22 (adds new-window/split/zoom)
40	declare -a tier1=(
41	  ""             ""  ""
42	  "New window"   c   "new-window -c '#{pane_current_path}'"
43	  "Split |"      "|" "split-window -h -c '#{pane_current_path}'"
44	  "Split -"      "-" "split-window -v -c '#{pane_current_path}'"
45	  "Zoom"         z   "resize-pane -Z"
46	)
47	
48	# Tier 2: submenus + cheatsheet (always shown if Tier 1 is shown)
49	declare -a tier2=(
50	  ""             ""  ""
51	  "→ Layouts"    L   "run-shell '$DIR/menu-layouts.sh'"
52	  "→ Session"    S   "run-shell '$DIR/menu-session.sh'"
53	  "→ Sesh+"      E   "run-shell '$DIR/menu-sesh.sh'"
54	  "→ Agents"     A   "run-shell '$DIR/menu-agents.sh'"
55	  "→ Popups"     o   "run-shell '$DIR/menu-popups.sh'"
56	  "→ Theme"      T   "run-shell '$DIR/menu-theme.sh'"
57	  "→ System"     Y   "run-shell '$DIR/menu-system.sh'"
58	  ""             ""  ""
59	  "Cheatsheet"   "?" "display-popup -E -w 80% -h 80% -T ' tmux cheatsheet ' 'glow -p $DIR/cheatsheet.md 2>/dev/null || less $DIR/cheatsheet.md'"
60	  "Search keys"  "/" "run-shell -b ~/.tmux/plugins/tmux-fzf/scripts/keybinding.sh"
61	)
62	
63	rows=("${tier0[@]}")
64	if [ "$H" -ge 22 ]; then
65	  rows+=("${tier1[@]}" "${tier2[@]}")
66	elif [ "$H" -ge 14 ]; then
67	  rows+=("${tier2[@]}")
68	fi
69	
70	exec tmux display-menu -T "#[align=centre,bold]tmux (h=$H)" -x R -y P "${rows[@]}"
71

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# upgrade_tools.sh — explicit, opt-in upgrade entrypoint.
3	#
4	# `chezmoi apply` is deliberately conservative (install-only, `state: present`,
5	# `creates:` idempotency). This script is the companion upgrade path: run it
6	# (or `just upgrade-*`) when you want to actually move tools forward.
7	#
8	# Design: each category is best-effort. A failure in one category does NOT
9	# abort later categories; a summary is printed at the end listing SUCCESS /
10	# FAILED / SKIPPED categories.
11	#
12	# Usage:
13	#   scripts/upgrade_tools.sh [all|<category> ...] [flags]
14	#
15	# Categories (also selectable via `all`):
16	#   externals brew mise uv npm cargo dotnet gem agents plugins
17	#
18	# Flags:
19	#   --dry-run          Print commands without executing.
20	#   --only a,b,c       Only run listed categories (comma-separated).
21	#   --skip a,b         Run everything except listed categories.
22	#   -h, --help         Show help.
23	#
24	# See docs/this_repo/upgrades.md and `## Upgrades` in AGENTS.md for rationale.
25	
26	set -u
27	# NOTE: we deliberately do not `set -e`. Each command is guarded by _run /
28	# run_category so we can continue past individual failures.
29	
30	# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
31	# Colors + loggers (match the style used in run_onchange_after_*.sh.tmpl)
32	# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
33	if [[ -t 1 ]]; then
34	  _C_RED='\033[0;31m'
35	  _C_GRN='\033[0;32m'
36	  _C_YLW='\033[1;33m'
37	  _C_BLU='\033[0;34m'
38	  _C_DIM='\033[2m'
39	  _C_RST='\033[0m'
40	else
41	  _C_RED='' _C_GRN='' _C_YLW='' _C_BLU='' _C_DIM='' _C_RST=''
42	fi
43	
44	info() { printf '%b\n' "${_C_BLU}[INFO]${_C_RST} $*"; }
45	success() { printf '%b\n' "${_C_GRN}[SUCCESS]${_C_RST} $*"; }
46	warn() { printf '%b\n' "${_C_YLW}[WARN]${_C_RST} $*"; }
47	error() { printf '%b\n' "${_C_RED}[ERROR]${_C_RST} $*" >&2; }
48	hr() { printf '%b\n' "${_C_DIM}────────────────────────────────────────────${_C_RST}"; }
49	
50	# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
51	# Source shared sudo helper (same file used by run_*.sh.tmpl via `include`)
52	# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
53	_REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
54	# shellcheck source=lib/sudo_shared.sh
55	if [[ -f "$_REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/sudo_shared.sh" ]]; then
56	  # shellcheck disable=SC1091
57	  source "$_REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/sudo_shared.sh"
58	fi
59	
60	# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
61	# Homebrew PATH detection (mirrors .chezmoiscripts/global/run_onchange_after_30_brew_bundle.sh.tmpl)
62	# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
63	setup_brew_path() {
64	  if command -v brew >/dev/null 2>&1; then
65	    return 0
66	  fi
67	  local candidates=(
68	    /opt/homebrew/bin/brew              # macOS Apple Silicon
69	    /usr/local/bin/brew                 # macOS Intel
70	    /home/linuxbrew/.linuxbrew/bin/brew # Linuxbrew system-wide
71	    "$HOME/.linuxbrew/bin/brew"         # Linuxbrew user
72	  )
73	  for b in "${candidates[@]}"; do
74	    if [[ -x "$b" ]]; then
75	      eval "$("$b" shellenv)"
76	      return 0
77	    fi
78	  done
79	  return 1
80	}
81	
82	# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
83	# Argument parsing
84	# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
85	DRY_RUN=0
86	ONLY=""
87	SKIP=""
88	SELECTED=()
89	
90	ALL_CATEGORIES=(externals brew mise uv npm cargo dotnet gem flatpak warp agents plugins)
91	
92	usage() {

94	Usage: scripts/upgrade_tools.sh [all|<category> ...] [--dry-run] [--only a,b] [--skip a,b]
95	
96	Categories: ${ALL_CATEGORIES[*]}
97	
98	Run order for 'all': ${ALL_CATEGORIES[*]}

# Add Charm CLI tools (gum, vhs, freeze) + evaluate mods/crush

## Context

Repo already uses `charmbracelet/glow` (markdown renderer, installed via
`dot_ansible/roles/devtools/tasks/main.yml`). User wants to add more
Charm tools they'd actually use day-to-day. After surveying ChatGPT's
recommendations against the repo's existing infrastructure:

- **gum** — clear, immediate value: 4 concrete spots in this repo's own
  scripts could use it (`tmux menu.sh` tier system, `menu-theme.sh`,
  `scripts/import_ssh_to_bw.sh` `read`-prompts, `scripts/upgrade_tools.sh`
  no-interactive-mode). User chose "install only, no refactor" — so we
  install now, refactor later when concrete need shows up.
- **vhs / freeze** — speculative but cheap. Currently zero `.tape` files
  and zero GIFs in `docs/`. Installing unblocks future demo recording for
  flows like `fleet-apply`, `sesh + tmux`, `tv agent-panes`.
- **mods / crush** — separately evaluated below; not auto-installed.

Goal: install the three CLIs cross-platform via the repo's existing
patterns (macOS Homebrew list + Linux GitHub-release fallback), document
them, and update all the cross-file mirrors `CLAUDE.md` requires.

---

## What to install

### Tier 1 — install in this PR

| Tool | Purpose | macOS | Linux |
|---|---|---|---|
| `gum` | Shell-script-friendly prompts (`gum choose`, `input`, `confirm`, `spin`, `filter`, `format`, `style`) | brew | GitHub release → `~/.local/bin/gum` |
| `vhs` | Record terminal sessions to GIF/MP4 from `.tape` script | brew | GitHub release → `~/.local/bin/vhs` |
| `freeze` | Code / terminal-output → static image (PNG/SVG) | brew | GitHub release → `~/.local/bin/freeze` |

### Tier 2 — out of scope (decision documented, not installed)

- **`mods`** — CLI LLM client. Skip: repo already has `aicapture` /
  `aisuggest` ecosystem (`dot_config/zsh/tools/04_ai_capture.zsh`,
  `05_aisuggest.zsh`) wrapping Claude / OpenCode / Codex / Cursor with
  per-agent model overrides (`AICAP_*_MODEL` env vars). `mods` would
  duplicate functionality without integrating with the existing
  agent-detection chain. Will add a one-paragraph note to
  `docs/tools/aicapture.md` explaining the deliberate non-choice.
- **`crush`** — Charm's agentic coding CLI. Skip: repo already manages
  4 coding-agent CLI overlays (Claude / OpenCode / Codex / Cursor) via
  `modify_` chezmoi prefix in `dot_claude/`, `dot_config/opencode/`,
  `dot_codex/`, `dot_cursor/`. The cost-of-ownership of each agent
  overlay is non-trivial (hook-aware mergers, TOML round-tripping). If
  user later wants to try `crush`, the existing pattern at
  `docs/tools/agent-overlays.md` plus
  `dot_ansible/roles/coding_agents/tasks/main.yml` is the documented
  add-a-5th-agent path.

### Explicitly NOT in scope

- `bubble-tea`, `bubbles`, `lip-gloss`, `glamour`, `huh` — Go libraries,
  not CLIs. Not relevant for a dotfiles repo (would only matter if
  authoring Go TUI apps).
- `wish`, `soft-serve`, `skate` — server-side / SSH-app tools. No
  current need; user not running self-hosted Git or KV store.
- `pop` (email), `melt` (mnemonic backup) — niche, not requested.

---

## Files to modify

### 1. Ansible role — `dot_ansible/roles/devtools/tasks/main.yml`

**Module-level header comment** (line 3): add `gum, vhs, freeze` to the
end of the tool list.

**macOS Homebrew list** (lines 17–52): add `- gum`, `- vhs`, `- freeze`
to the `community.general.homebrew` `name:` list (alphabetically: `gum`
between `grc` and `htop`; `vhs` after `television`; `freeze` after
`eza`).

**Linux GitHub-release blocks** — append three new blocks following the
exact `glow` pattern at lines 1202–1310. For each tool, copy the
13-task block and rename. Per-tool details:

| Tool | Repo | Asset name template | Binary inside |
|---|---|---|---|
| `gum` | `charmbracelet/gum` | `gum_<ver>_Linux_<arch>.tar.gz` | `gum` |
| `vhs` | `charmbracelet/vhs` | `vhs_<ver>_Linux_<arch>.tar.gz` | `vhs` |
| `freeze` | `charmbracelet/freeze` | `freeze_<ver>_Linux_<arch>.tar.gz` | `freeze` |

Architecture mapping is identical to `glow` (x86_64/arm64/arm). All
three follow `charmbracelet`'s standard release naming, so the glow
block's URL template `…/{{ tag }}/<tool>_{{ ver }}_Linux_{{ arch }}.tar.gz`
works as-is.

**Important**: keep `rescue:` block on each (network-timeout
tolerance) — see `glow` lines 1304–1310.

**Note on `vhs` runtime deps**: `vhs` requires `ttyd` and `ffmpeg` at
runtime to actually record. On Linux, both are usually missing. The
ansible block will install the binary; runtime deps documented in
`docs/tools/vhs.md` as a "before first use" step. Don't auto-install
`ttyd`/`ffmpeg` — they're heavy and `vhs` is opt-in.

### 2. Tool docs — three new pages under `docs/tools/`

Create:

- `docs/tools/gum.md` (~200 lines) — `gum choose / input / confirm /
  spin / filter / format / style` with concrete examples reusing patterns
  from this repo's own scripts (so the doc doubles as a "here's where
  it would slot in" hint when refactor time comes). Cross-link from
  `docs/tools/tmux/keybindings.md` (mention as alternative to
  `display-menu` for ≥14-row menus).
- `docs/tools/vhs.md` (~150 lines) — install, runtime deps
  (ttyd/ffmpeg), `.tape` script syntax, recording a demo. Note that
  the repo doesn't yet have any `.tape` files; section "Where to put
  tapes" suggests `docs/_demos/*.tape` if/when used.
- `docs/tools/freeze.md` (~120 lines) — `freeze main.py -o code.png`,
  flags for theme/font, integration with `bat` for syntax highlighting.

Each page's structure follows the established template from
`docs/tools/fzf.md` / `docs/tools/direnv.md`: title + upstream link, why
in this repo, install verification, examples, troubleshooting.

**Optional page** — `docs/tools/glow.md` (~80 lines): repo uses glow but
has no docs page. Could be a small bonus addition since we're touching
this surface anyway. **Decision**: include it, since the per-page cost is
low and `mkdocs.yml` will need a new section anyway. Cross-link from
`docs/tools/web-reader.md` (which already mentions glow at line 11).

### 3. zh-TW translations

Per the existing pattern (every English page has a `.zh-TW.md` sibling —
visible in the `ls docs/tools/` output: 39 pages × 2 languages), each
new page needs a `.zh-TW.md` translation. Follow the "preserve English
originals for proper nouns / commands / file paths" rule from the
`mkdocs-site-bootstrap` skill that bootstrapped this repo's i18n.

### 4. `mkdocs.yml` nav

Insert under the existing `Tools → Shell & terminal` block (line ~213):

\```yaml
- Shell & terminal:
    - Ghostty: tools/ghostty.md
    - Warp: tools/warp.md
    - Starship: tools/starship.md
    - Clipboard: tools/clipboard.md

    - TV vs fzf: tools/tv-vs-fzf.md
    - Glow (markdown reader): tools/glow.md       # NEW
    - Gum (shell prompts): tools/gum.md           # NEW
    - VHS (terminal demo recorder): tools/vhs.md  # NEW
    - Freeze (code → image): tools/freeze.md      # NEW
\```

Order: existing alpha-ish-but-narrative ordering keeps fzf/tv together;
glow/gum/vhs/freeze form a natural Charm cluster at the end.

### 5. `README.md`

Update line 239 — the "Dev tools" list under "What You Get". Add `gum,
vhs, freeze` to the comma-separated list (after `glow`, since they're
the same upstream).

Add nothing else to README — the tools don't appear in macOS-only
playbooks, ansible role headers, or the "Quick Setup" flow.

### 6. `CLAUDE.md` — no change required

The cross-file maintenance rules already cover what we're doing
(devtools role → README.md, new docs page → mkdocs.yml). Nothing here
graduates to a hard invariant.

### 7. Cross-link from `docs/tools/aicapture.md`

Add a one-paragraph "Why not Charm `mods`?" note (≤6 lines) explaining
the deliberate skip. Lives near the top of the page where the
multi-agent chain is described. Same for `crush` if there's a natural
spot in `docs/tools/agent-overlays.md`.

## Verification

After implementation, run all of these and confirm clean output:

\```bash

# 3. Apply on the local machine and verify binaries land
chezmoi apply
which gum vhs freeze glow            # all 4 should resolve

# 4. Smoke-test gum interactively

echo "name: $(gum input --placeholder 'demo')"

# 5. Smoke-test freeze (no runtime deps needed)

freeze /tmp/hello.py -o /tmp/hello.png && file /tmp/hello.png

# 6. Smoke-test vhs only if ttyd+ffmpeg available
command -v ttyd && command -v ffmpeg && {
  cat <<'TAPE' > /tmp/demo.tape
Output /tmp/demo.gif
Set FontSize 18
Type "echo hello vhs"
Enter
Sleep 1s
TAPE
  vhs /tmp/demo.tape && file /tmp/demo.gif
}

# 7. Linux: verify GitHub-release path actually picks the right asset
# Run on a Linux host:

## Approved Plan:
# Add Charm CLI tools (gum, vhs, freeze) + evaluate mods/crush

## Context

Repo already uses `charmbracelet/glow` (markdown renderer, installed via
`dot_ansible/roles/devtools/tasks/main.yml`). User wants to add more
Charm tools they'd actually use day-to-day. After surveying ChatGPT's
recommendations against the repo's existing infrastructure:

- **gum** — clear, immediate value: 4 concrete spots in this repo's own
  scripts could use it (`tmux menu.sh` tier system, `menu-theme.sh`,
  `scripts/import_ssh_to_bw.sh` `read`-prompts, `scripts/upgrade_tools.sh`
  no-interactive-mode). User chose "install only, no refactor" — so we
  install now, refactor later when concrete need shows up.
- **vhs / freeze** — speculative but cheap. Currently zero `.tape` files
  and zero GIFs in `docs/`. Installing unblocks future demo recording for
  flows like `fleet-apply`, `sesh + tmux`, `tv agent-panes`.
- **mods / crush** — separately evaluated below; not auto-installed.

Goal: install the three CLIs cross-platform via the repo's existing
patterns (macOS Homebrew list + Linux GitHub-release fallback), document
them, and update all the cross-file mirrors `CLAUDE.md` requires.

---

## What to install

### Tier 1 — install in this PR

| Tool | Purpose | macOS | Linux |
|---|---|---|---|
| `gum` | Shell-script-friendly prompts (`gum choose`, `input`, `confirm`, `spin`, `filter`, `format`, `style`) | brew | GitHub release → `~/.local/bin/gum` |
| `vhs` | Record terminal sessions to GIF/MP4 from `.tape` script | brew | GitHub release → `~/.local/bin/vhs` |
| `freeze` | Code / terminal-output → static image (PNG/SVG) | brew | GitHub release → `~/.local/bin/freeze` |

### Tier 2 — out of scope (decision documented, not installed)

- **`mods`** — CLI LLM client. Skip: repo already has `aicapture` /
  `aisuggest` ecosystem (`dot_config/zsh/tools/04_ai_capture.zsh`,
  `05_aisuggest.zsh`) wrapping Claude / OpenCode / Codex / Cursor with
  per-agent model overrides (`AICAP_*_MODEL` env vars). `mods` would
  duplicate functionality without integrating with the existing
  agent-detection chain. Will add a one-paragraph note to
  `docs/tools/aicapture.md` explaining the deliberate non-choice.
- **`crush`** — Charm's agentic coding CLI. Skip: repo already manages
  4 coding-agent CLI overlays (Claude / OpenCode / Codex / Cursor) via
  `modify_` chezmoi prefix in `dot_claude/`, `dot_config/opencode/`,
  `dot_codex/`, `dot_cursor/`. The cost-of-ownership of each agent
  overlay is non-trivial (hook-aware mergers, TOML round-tripping). If
  user later wants to try `crush`, the existing pattern at
  `docs/tools/agent-overlays.md` plus
  `dot_ansible/roles/coding_agents/tasks/main.yml` is the documented
  add-a-5th-agent path.

### Explicitly NOT in scope

- `bubble-tea`, `bubbles`, `lip-gloss`, `glamour`, `huh` — Go libraries,
  not CLIs. Not relevant for a dotfiles repo (would only matter if
  authoring Go TUI apps).
- `wish`, `soft-serve`, `skate` — server-side / SSH-app tools. No
  current need; user not running self-hosted Git or KV store.
- `pop` (email), `melt` (mnemonic backup) — niche, not requested.

---

## Files to modify

### 1. Ansible role — `dot_ansible/roles/devtools/tasks/main.yml`

**Module-level header comment** (line 3): add `gum, vhs, freeze` to the
end of the tool list.

**macOS Homebrew list** (lines 17–52): add `- gum`, `- vhs`, `- freeze`
to the `community.general.homebrew` `name:` list (alphabetically: `gum`
between `grc` and `htop`; `vhs` after `television`; `freeze` after
`eza`).

**Linux GitHub-release blocks** — append three new blocks following the
exact `glow` pattern at lines 1202–1310. For each tool, copy the
13-task block and rename. Per-tool details:

| Tool | Repo | Asset name template | Binary inside |
|---|---|---|---|
| `gum` | `charmbracelet/gum` | `gum_<ver>_Linux_<arch>.tar.gz` | `gum` |
| `vhs` | `charmbracelet/vhs` | `vhs_<ver>_Linux_<arch>.tar.gz` | `vhs` |
| `freeze` | `charmbracelet/freeze` | `freeze_<ver>_Linux_<arch>.tar.gz` | `freeze` |

Architecture mapping is identical to `glow` (x86_64/arm64/arm). All
three follow `charmbracelet`'s standard release naming, so the glow
block's URL template `…/{{ tag }}/<tool>_{{ ver }}_Linux_{{ arch }}.tar.gz`
works as-is.

**Important**: keep `rescue:` block on each (network-timeout
tolerance) — see `glow` lines 1304–1310.

**Note on `vhs` runtime deps**: `vhs` requires `ttyd` and `ffmpeg` at
runtime to actually record. On Linux, both are usually missing. The
ansible block will install the binary; runtime deps documented in
`docs/tools/vhs.md` as a "before first use" step. Don't auto-install
`ttyd`/`ffmpeg` — they're heavy and `vhs` is opt-in.

### 2. Tool docs — three new pages under `docs/tools/`

- `docs/tools/gum.md` (~200 lines) — `gum choose / input / confirm /

  `display-menu` for ≥14-row menus).
- `docs/tools/vhs.md` (~150 lines) — install, runtime deps

  tapes" suggests `docs/_demos/*.tape` if/when used.
- `docs/tools/freeze.md` (~120 lines) — `freeze main.py -o code.png`,

Each page's structure follows the established template from

**Optional page** — `docs/tools/glow.md` (~80 lines): repo uses glow but

1	# direnv
2	
3	`direnv` loads per-project environment variables as you enter and leave directories. In this repo it is initialized from Zsh, while prompt display is handled by Starship.
4	
5	- **Helper file**: `~/.config/direnv/direnvrc` (chezmoi source: `dot_config/direnv/direnvrc`)
6	- **Zsh init**: `~/.config/zsh/tools/30_direnv.zsh`
7	- **Prompt**: `~/.config/starship.toml` via Starship's `[python]` module
8	
9	## Python `.venv` helper
10	
11	This repo provides `layout_python_venv [venv_dir=.venv]`.
12	
13	- Activates an existing virtual environment directory
14	- Does not auto-create `.venv`
15	- Delegates activation to `layout python3`
16	- Watches the venv marker files so creating `.venv` later triggers a reload on the next prompt
17	
18	## Recommended `.envrc`
19	
20	```sh
21	layout_python_venv
22	dotenv_if_exists
23	```
24	
25	Then allow it once per project:
26	
27	```bash
28	direnv allow
29	```
30	
31	You can target a non-default virtual environment directory if needed:
32	
33	```sh
34	layout_python_venv venv
35	dotenv_if_exists
36	```
37	
38	## Behavior Notes
39	
40	- Equivalent for daily use: `VIRTUAL_ENV`, `PATH`, and `PYTHONHOME` handling come from direnv's built-in `layout python3`
41	- Not fully equivalent to `source .venv/bin/activate`: no `deactivate()` shell function and no direct `PS1` rewriting
42	- Prompt display still works because Starship reads `VIRTUAL_ENV` and shows the active environment name
43	- Leaving the directory automatically restores the previous environment
44	
45	## References
46	
47	- [Python · direnv Wiki](https://github.com/direnv/direnv/wiki/Python)
48	- [Activate python venv by default? · Issue #1264](https://github.com/direnv/direnv/issues/1264)
49	- [PS1 · direnv Wiki](https://github.com/direnv/direnv/wiki/PS1)
50

```md
# Glow — terminal Markdown reader

[charmbracelet/glow](https://github.com/charmbracelet/glow) renders Markdown in the terminal with syntax highlighting and pager support. In this repo it powers the tmux cheatsheet popup and the `readurl` / `readlocal` web-reader pipeline.

- **Install**:
  - macOS — Homebrew (managed by `dot_ansible/roles/devtools/tasks/main.yml` macOS list)
  - Linux — GitHub release tarball into `~/.local/bin/glow` (managed by `dot_ansible/roles/devtools/tasks/main.yml` `# --- glow ---` block)
- **Used by**:
  - tmux popup menu cheatsheet — `prefix + Space` → `?` (see `dot_config/tmux/executable_menu.sh`)
  - Web reader pipeline — `readurl` / `readlocal` / `readnode` / `readraw` (see [Web reader](web-reader.md))
  - `aicapture` agent output rendering when stdout is markdown-shaped

---

## Daily commands

\```bash
# Render a file with the pager (q to quit, j/k to scroll)
glow -p README.md

# Render a remote file
glow https://raw.githubusercontent.com/foo/bar/main/README.md

# Pipe markdown through (no pager, just rendered)
echo '# hello\n- a\n- b' | glow

# Width-constrained for narrow terminals
glow -w 80 README.md

# Choose a style explicitly
glow -s dark README.md     # dark | light | notty | <path-to-json>
\```

The pager (`-p`) uses the same `bat`-style scroll keys most of the team already knows, so `glow -p file.md` is the closest equivalent to `bat README.md` for prose.

---

## Recommended aliases

This repo doesn't bind a global glow alias because the various callers (tmux cheatsheet, web reader) call it directly with the right flags. If you want a personal alias, add it to a private zsh fragment:

\```bash
# ~/.config/zsh/tools/99_local.zsh (gitignored)
alias mdv='glow -p'
alias mdvw='glow -w "$(($(tput cols) - 4))" -p'
\```

---

## Tips

- **TUI mode** — `glow` (no args) launches a TUI file browser for the current directory; arrow keys to navigate, `Enter` to open. Use `glow -a` to also list dotfiles.
- **Stash** — Charm offers a hosted stash for marking docs you read often. We don't use the hosted side; if you do, `glow stash add <file>` and `glow stash` to list.
- **Style files** — Glow accepts a path to a JSON style for full theming. The repo's tmux cheatsheet relies on the default dark style, which works on both Catppuccin and tmux2k tmux themes.
- **Fallback** — When `glow` isn't installed (e.g., during early bootstrap on a new machine), the tmux menu falls back to `less`. See `dot_config/tmux/executable_menu.sh` row `Cheatsheet` for the `glow … 2>/dev/null || less …` pattern.

---

## See also

- [Web reader](web-reader.md) — `readurl`, `readlocal`, `readnode`, `readraw`
- [tmux overview](tmux/README.md) — popup menu and cheatsheet
- [Gum](gum.md), [VHS](vhs.md), [Freeze](freeze.md) — the rest of the Charm CLI ecosystem in this repo

```md
# Gum — shell-script-friendly TUI prompts

[charmbracelet/gum](https://github.com/charmbracelet/gum) is a single-binary toolbox of TUI primitives (`choose`, `input`, `confirm`, `spin`, `filter`, `format`, `style`, `write`, `pager`) for use inside shell scripts. It bundles the same Bubble Tea / Bubbles / Lip Gloss UI behind a CLI, so scripts can have polished interactive UX without dragging in a Go build.

- **Install**:
  - macOS — Homebrew (managed by `dot_ansible/roles/devtools/tasks/main.yml` macOS list)
  - Linux — GitHub release tarball into `~/.local/bin/gum` (managed by `dot_ansible/roles/devtools/tasks/main.yml` `# --- gum (Charm) ---` block)
- **Verify**: `gum --version`
- **Status in this repo**: installed, not yet wired into existing scripts. See [Where it would fit](#where-it-would-fit-future-refactors) below.

---

## Cheat sheet

\```bash
# Pick one
choice=$(gum choose --header "Pick action" "train" "test" "deploy")

# Pick many (space toggles, enter confirms)
items=$(gum choose --no-limit --header "Pick keys to import" id_rsa github_key work_key)

# Free-text input
name=$(gum input --placeholder "experiment name" --prompt "▸ ")

# Multi-line input
notes=$(gum write --placeholder "release notes (Ctrl+D when done)")

# Yes/no
gum confirm "Run now?" && ./run.sh

# Filter a list with fuzzy search (think gum-flavored fzf)
host=$(printf '%s\n' alpha beta gamma | gum filter --placeholder "host…")

# Spinner around a long command
gum spin --title "Building…" --spinner dot -- bash -c 'sleep 3 && echo done'

# Style standalone text
gum style --foreground 212 --border double --padding "1 2" "Hello $USER"

# Format markdown / code in-line
gum format -- "# Header" "" "- bullet **bold**"

# Page through long output (alternative to less)
some-long-command | gum pager
\```

`gum --help` lists every subcommand; each subcommand has its own `--help` with all flags.

---

## Why it pairs well with this dotfiles repo

- **No Bash boilerplate** — replaces `read -p` / `select` / hand-rolled menus with one-liners that already handle keyboard navigation, escape-to-cancel, and reasonable defaults.
- **Single static binary** — installs identically on macOS / Linux / WSL via Homebrew or GitHub release; same script works everywhere.
- **Composable with pipes** — every output goes to stdout, so `gum choose | xargs -I{} …` plugs straight into existing pipelines.
- **Honors `NO_COLOR`** — falls back to plain output when stdout isn't a TTY or `NO_COLOR=1` is set, so scripts can be piped without breakage.

---

## Common patterns

### `gum choose` for menus that outgrow tmux's `display-menu`

The tmux popup menu (`dot_config/tmux/executable_menu.sh`) currently uses a tier-based fallback to fight tmux's silent-fail-when-too-tall bug (see `pitfalls/tmux-display-menu-silent-fail.md`). `gum choose` has no row cap and renders the same menu without tiering:

\```bash
# Instead of `tmux display-menu -T '...' "Last window" Tab last-window …`
choice=$(gum choose --header "tmux menu" --height 20 \
  "Last window" "Last pane" "Choose window" "Choose session" \
  "Pane numbers" "Sesh picker" "Lazygit" "New window" \
  "Split |" "Split -" "Zoom" "→ Layouts" "→ Theme" "→ Cheatsheet")
case "$choice" in
  "Last window") tmux last-window ;;
  …
esac
\```

### `gum confirm` instead of `read -r yes_no`

\```bash
# Before
read -r -p "Overwrite [y/N]? " ans
[[ "$ans" =~ ^[Yy] ]] && do_thing

# After
gum confirm --default=No "Overwrite?" && do_thing
\```

### `gum spin` to silence a noisy long-runner

\```bash
# Hide the chatty output of a slow command behind a spinner
gum spin --show-output --title "chezmoi apply" -- chezmoi apply -v
\```

`--show-output` keeps stdout streaming under the spinner; drop it to fully suppress.

### `gum input --password` for secrets

\```bash
# Reads without echoing; pipe straight into a sudo helper
gum input --password --placeholder "sudo password" \
  | install -m 0600 /dev/stdin /tmp/sudo-pass
\```

### `gum filter` as an `fzf` alternative for one-shot pickers

`fzf` is still the right tool for ZLE keybindings (`Ctrl+T`, `Ctrl+R`) — its preview window and bindings are tighter. `gum filter` shines when you want consistent Charm styling inside a script that already uses other gum primitives.

---

## Where it would fit (future refactors)

These spots in the repo are documented as gum candidates but were intentionally left untouched in the install PR. When you next touch them, consider the swap:

| File | Current UX | gum sketch |
|---|---|---|
| `dot_config/tmux/executable_menu.sh` | tier-based `display-menu` (~14-row cap) | `gum choose --height N` |
| `dot_config/tmux/executable_menu-theme.sh` | 2-row `display-menu` | `gum choose "catppuccin" "tmux2k"` |
| `scripts/import_ssh_to_bw.sh` | `read -r choice` + manual parse | `gum choose --no-limit` + `gum confirm` |
| `scripts/upgrade_tools.sh` | CLI args only | `gum choose --no-limit` for category multi-select when called with no args |

Don't bulk-refactor — the existing scripts work, and tmux integration in particular has subtle invariants (see `CLAUDE.md` → "Tmux ≥ 3.3 required for popup menu"). Swap one at a time, when you're already in the file for another reason.

---

## Environment / styling

Gum reads `GUM_*` env vars to set defaults globally. Useful ones:

\```bash
# In ~/.config/zsh/tools/99_local.zsh (private)
export GUM_INPUT_CURSOR_FOREGROUND="#FF6188"
export GUM_INPUT_PROMPT_FOREGROUND="#A9DC76"
export GUM_CHOOSE_CURSOR_FOREGROUND="#FFD866"
\```

Full list: `gum --help` after each subcommand. The repo doesn't ship gum-wide defaults — keep them user-local so SSH sessions to other hosts inherit the upstream defaults.

---

## Tips

- **Cancellation** — `Esc` cancels and exits with non-zero. Always use `set -o pipefail` or check the exit code: `choice=$(gum choose …) || exit 0`.
- **Empty arrays** — `gum choose --no-limit` with nothing selected exits 0 with empty stdout. Guard with `[[ -n "$choice" ]] || exit 0`.
- **TTY detection** — gum auto-disables interactivity when stdin isn't a TTY (e.g., inside a pipe). For tests, pass `--height` and pre-feed stdin via heredoc.
- **In tmux popups** — `gum choose` works inside `tmux display-popup -E -- gum choose …`. Use `-w 60% -h 60%` to size the popup.

---

## See also

- [Glow](glow.md), [VHS](vhs.md), [Freeze](freeze.md) — the rest of the Charm CLI ecosystem
- [Fzf](fzf.md) — the established fuzzy-finder; complementary, not replaced
- [tmux overview](tmux/README.md) — popup menus and the `display-menu` height limit

```
